questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2012
questions.questionText:
6.
The Boghaz Koi inscription from Asia Minor
refers to the following Vedic deities:
questions.explanation:
The Boghaz Koi Inscription from asia minor
refers to vedic deities Indra, mitra, varuna and Nasatyas.
The Boghaz Koi inscription of about 1400 B.C. refer to
certain contracts between king of Hittites (in persia) and
the king of mitani. In this Inscription Indra, Varuna,
Mitra and Nasatya are mentioned as the protectors of
contracts.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2012
questions.questionText:
7.
To which of the following tribes did King
Sudasa, described in the Rigveda as having
defeated ten Kings, belong?
questions.explanation:
King Sudasa described in the Rigveda as
having defeated ten kings belong to Tritsu tribe the
Battle of ten kings was fought between king Sudasa and
other ten king (5 Aryans & 5 non Aryans). Sudasa was
victor in this battle. This Battle is mentioned in seventh
Book of Rigveda. This Battle was fought on the Bank of
Parushni (Now Ravi) river. Puru were the main in
defeated tribes.

Who had made the following statement?

'Bhagavapi
Khatrio
Ahampi
khatrio'
(Bhagawan [Buddha] was a Kshatriya I too am
a kshatriya).
questions.explanation:
Ajatasatru stated "Bhagavapi khatrio Ahampi
Khatrio" (Bhagvan Buddha) was kshatriya. I am too
kshatriya)
 Ajatasatru ruled Magadha from 492 BC- 460BC. In
his ruling period First Buddhist council was held in
saptaparni cave of Rajgriha. In this council teachings of
Buddha were compiled in sutta pitaka and vinaya
pitaka.

mentioned about the hoarded wealth of the
rulers of the Nanda dynasty?

the sangam literature attributed to mamulanar including
verse 8 of the Tiruvalluva malai. Mamulanar has also
described about the destruction of Pataliputra by river
Ganges.

Khalji?
questions.explanation:
In 1303, a mongol army from chagatai
khanate launched an invasion of Delhi sultanate.

ransacked its suburbs ultimately they decided to retreat
having been unable to breach Alauddin's camp.

first time used in Muslim architecture in India?
questions.explanation:
The nine cusped arches were for the first
time used in Buildings of shah Jahan. Sahjahan's period
is called "golden age for Architecture". Main
architecture built by shahjahan are Diwan-i-Aam
(1627), Diwan-i-khas (1637), moti mosque (1654), Red
fort (1648) and Taj mahal.

historians. Hayden White attacked the concept of
causation as depriving people of both their freedom
of action in the present them in an inescapable
network of causation. Postmodernist theory installs
interpretation in the place of empirical research into
the causes of specific events.

time, some postmodernists attack the latter too. The
cause of an occurrence must obviously come before it
in time. But the postmodernist historian and
philosopher, Ankersmit, says "Historical time is a
writing of historical narrative based on the concept
of time, what he has declared, is "building on
quicksand." The postmodernists would prefer that
the idea of sequential time be abandoned in the
writing of history.

Richard Evans shows how the very idea of
postmodern is paradoxical in that it is contrary to the
assertion that there are no time periods in history.
And the postmodernist statement that historical time
is a thing of the past, itself uses the historical concept
of time which the statement is intended to dismiss.
The linear and sequential concept of time is far too
powerful a principle to be dispensed with, for it is not
an intellectual construct but a matter of everyday
experience for people the world over. Time itself may
be without boundaries, but in terms of human life it
passes, and has limits.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2012
questions.questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and choose the
correct answer of the questions that follow (Q. No. 71
to 75):

Causation is a concept of such fundamental
importance to historical understanding that E.H.
Carr in his G.M. Trevelyan lectures (1961) declared
the study of history to be the study of causes. But
postmodernist thinking on the issue of historical
causation is different. John Vincent would abandon
the search for causes as futile and rather look for
causes as futile and rather look for explanations.
Writing in 1976. Theodore Zeldin thought of
causation and chronology as the two tyrants to
historians. Hayden White attacked the concept of
causation as depriving people of both their freedom
of action in the present them in an inescapable
network of causation. Postmodernist theory installs
interpretation in the place of empirical research into
the causes of specific events.

Since the notion of cause depends on sequential
time, some postmodernists attack the latter too. The
cause of an occurrence must obviously come before it
in time. But the postmodernist historian and
philosopher, Ankersmit, says "Historical time is a
writing of historical narrative based on the concept
of time, what he has declared, is "building on
quicksand." The postmodernists would prefer that
the idea of sequential time be abandoned in the
writing of history.

Richard Evans shows how the very idea of
postmodern is paradoxical in that it is contrary to the
assertion that there are no time periods in history.
And the postmodernist statement that historical time
is a thing of the past, itself uses the historical concept
of time which the statement is intended to dismiss.
The linear and sequential concept of time is far too
powerful a principle to be dispensed with, for it is not
an intellectual construct but a matter of everyday
experience for people the world over. Time itself may
be without boundaries, but in terms of human life it
passes, and has limits.

74. Who amongst the following wrote that the
cause-effect relationship is an obstacle for
History?
questions.explanation:
Theodore Zeldin wrote that the cause effect
relationship is an obstacle for history

questions.explanation:
Panchajana in Rigveda refers to the five
tribes of Aryans. Five tribes were Anu, Druhya, Puru,
Turwas and Yadu.
* Jana, word is mentioned in Rigveda 275 times.

Rigveda for promoting agriculture?
questions.explanation:
Four reasons are mentioned in the Rigveda
for promoting agriculture.

coins for the first time in India?
questions.explanation:
Kushan ruler Vima Kadphises issued gold
coins for the first time in India. He ruled from about 90-
100 C.E.
* Kushan empire was founded by Kujula Kadphises.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2011 (Shift 1) Paper II
questions.questionText:
5. Who among the following Kings was the first to
issue a long inscription in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation:
Rudradaman's Junagarh Inscription was the
first inscription in Sanskrit. The Inscription is dated
shortly after 150 C.E.
* The Junagarh rock contains inscriptions of Ashoka,
Rudradaman I and Skandagupta.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2011 (Shift 1) Paper II
questions.questionText:
6. Which of the following denotes the Bhukti in
the Gupta period?
questions.explanation:
Bhukti denotes provinces in the Gupta period.
Uparika was the head of Bhukti. Vishaya denotes
District. Mahattar Denotes Village.

questions.explanation:
Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi was written by Shams
Siraj Afif it gives a detailed account of the reign of
Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351-1388).

Masjid between 1650 and 1656 at the highest point of
Shah Jahanabad. The Mosque was designated by

workers.

Mahe was trading station of French. All other stations
Calicut, Mahe and cochin were in control of portuguese.

English at Buxar?

Mir Kasim fought with English at Buxar.
* Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between joint
Army of Shujauddaula, Shah Alam and Mir Kasim with
British Army. War concluded with treaty of Allahabad
1765.

questions.explanation:
Pitts India Act was passed in 1784 to rectify
the defects of Regulating act 1773. In this act-
1. The company's territories in India were for the first
time called the British possession in India.
2. British government was given the supreme control
over company's affairs and its administration in India.

Indian Association for the Cultivation of
Science?

Indian Association for the cultivation of
sciences is a public deemed research university for
higher education and research in Basic Sciences. It is
established by Mahendralal Sircar. It is Asia's oldest
research Institute located at Kolkata.

Punjabi Ghadrites on Board the Kamagata
Maru clashed with British army in Budge Budge.
Kamagata Maru incidence happened in 1914.

planning Commission of India established?
questions.explanation:
Planning commission of India was
established in 1950. The planning commission was set
up by a Resolution of government of India in March,
1950. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first chairman of
planning commission.

(Struggle for Italian Unification).

Which of the following games was known to the
people of the Indus Valley?
questions.explanation:
Game of dice was known to the people of
Indus valley. There is no evidence of use of horse in
Indus valley civilization. Only one terracota figure of
horse found from Surkotada. Chariot racing, polo and
horse riding needs horse. They did not used horses, so
they were not used to play these games.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History Dec 2011 Paper II

Which of the following did Mahavira the real
founder of Jainism-belong to?
questions.explanation:
Mahavir Swami belong to an aristocratic
family and Kshatriya clan called Jnatrika. He was born
in Kundagrama near Patna and his father was king of
that area. His mother Trishala was sister of Chetak an
eminent prince of Vaisali.
* Gautam Buddha belonged to Sakya clan.

the Brahmi script was not used?

Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra inscription of
Ashoka written in Kharoshthi script. Dhauli and Sarnath
inscription were written in Brahmi script. Shahbazgarhi
located in Pakistan. Dhauli inscription is situated in
Odisha.

Hegel's philosophy bridged the chasm separating
Christian scholars and secular philosophers. He provided
enough God to satisfy liberal Christians and an emphasis
on reason that appeased the rationalists. In the process,
he established new paradigms that swept through
academia. His macro-historical approach widened the
sphere of historical studies. It illustrated the benefits of
expanding the studies that had hitherto been limited to
political
history
and
biographical
works.
New
possibilities in social history were avidly accepted by
the next generation of historians, including Karl Marx.
Efforts were made to link separate histories into an all-
encompassing world history. Hegel's division of history
into four great epochs (the Oriental, the Greek, the
Roman and the German) convinced many historians that
different eras and cultures were fundamentally dissimilar
and had to be evaluated within their own contexts and in
recognition of the specific "needs of that age". Hegel's
insistence that motives often differed from those
professed, led to a more critical appraisal of source
materials. Actions, motives and repercussions were
increasingly scrutinized for consistency, and casual
relationships became more and more important. The
dialectic model had less immediate impact, but in later
generations it has become a staple tenet in many
historical interpretations.

enough God to satisfy liberal Christians and an emphasis
on reason that appeased the rationalists. In the process,
he established new paradigms that swept through
academia. His macro-historical approach widened the
sphere of historical studies. It illustrated the benefits of
expanding the studies that had hitherto been limited to
political
history
and
biographical
works.
New
possibilities in social history were avidly accepted by
the next generation of historians, including Karl Marx.
Efforts were made to link separate histories into an all-
encompassing world history. Hegel's division of history
into four great epochs (the Oriental, the Greek, the
Roman and the German) convinced many historians that
different eras and cultures were fundamentally dissimilar
and had to be evaluated within their own contexts and in
recognition of the specific "needs of that age". Hegel's
insistence that motives often differed from those
professed, led to a more critical appraisal of source
materials. Actions, motives and repercussions were
increasingly scrutinized for consistency, and casual
relationships became more and more important. The
dialectic model had less immediate impact, but in later
generations it has become a staple tenet in many
historical interpretations.

49. Hegel
expanded
history
writings
by
emphasizing on one of the following:
questions.explanation:
Hegel expanded history writings by
emphasizing on Social History.

defeated tribes.

The most vicious system of racial oppression was set up
in South Africa. The system of racial segregation, called
apartheid, was enforced in the country by the

do so. South Africa left the Commonwealth when the
policy of apartheid came under attack at the conference
of the Prime Ministers of Commonwealth countries.

worked incessantly to construct Taj Mahal.

between 1638 to 1663. He was a jweller and visited
India at the ruling period of Shahjahan. He has written
his memoirs titled “travels In India”. In this memoir he
has given vivid description of ruling period of
Shahjahan and Aurangzeb.

Jumla tried to monopolise trade in all important
commodities but (R) does not explain (A).

banned in 1910 by the British government in India as a
seditious text.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II

38. Who of the following was known as 'Socrates of
Maharashtra'?
questions.explanation:
M.G. Ranade was known as “Socrates of
Maharashtra”. Ranade was an Indian scholar, social
reformer, judge and Author. He helped to establish
Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Maharashtra Granthottejak
Sabha and Prarthna Samaj. He edited a Bombay anglo
Marathi news paper Induprakash. He was given title of
“Rao Bahadur”.

seats reserved for the depressed classes out of

questions.explanation:
As a result of Poona pact the number of seats
reserved for the depressed classes out of general
electorate seats were Increased. Poona pact was signed
in 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II
questions.questionText:
40. The Gujarat Sabha led by Gandhi played a
leading role in the
questions.explanation:
The Gujarat Sabha led by Gandhi played a
leading role in peasant agitation of kheda. In 1918, the
British Authorities had increased the taxes of Kheda
region by 23% while it was hit by chappania Famine
and cholera and plague. People revolted in leadership of
Gandhi. Govt. came on Back foot and tax of year 1918
and 1919 suspended. The increase in rate of taxes was
reduced.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II
questions.questionText:
41. Who of the following set up Mahila Arya
Samaj to improve Women's Education?
questions.explanation:
Pandita Ramabai started Arya Mahila Samaj
in 1881 in pune to improve the condition of women,
especially child widows. In 1889, she established the
Mukti Mission in Pune, a refuge for young widows who
had been deserted and abused by their families.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II
questions.questionText: 42. In which year Sharda Act was passed?
questions.explanation:
Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sharda Act)
was passed in 1929, in the imperial legislative council
of India. It fixed the age of marriage for girls at 14 years
and boys 18 years. It is popularly known as the Sharda
Act after its sponsorer Harbilas Sharda.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II

was from
questions.explanation:
Rani Gaidinliu who fought against the British
was from Nagaland. She was Imprisoned for life and
Jawaharlal Nehru made her free after Independence.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II
questions.questionText:

with Indian National Army?
questions.explanation:
Rasbihari Ghosh was not associated with
Indian national army. Rashbihari Ghosh was an Indian
politician, Lawyer, social worker and philanthropist. He
presided congress in 1907 in Surat session after which
the congress split into moderates and Extremist and then
the year after in madras 1908.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2013 Paper II
questions.questionText:
45. In February 1947 Prime Minister Attlee
declared that the British would quit India by
questions.explanation:
The Prime Minister of Britain, Clement Atlee
declared on Feb 20, 1947 in the house of commons that
the British would quit India after transferring power into
the responsible hand not later than June 1948. The idea
was that the Indians should settle their issues before
that. He also announced the appointment of Lord
Mountbatten as viceroy in place of Lord Wavell.

questions.explanation:
Before the scientific revolution of 17th

(A) Most of the writers were ignorant about the idea of

(B) The subject matter of history was treated more or

The recruitment of the company's army in the
eighteenth century was not just building on the existing
traditions of the North Indian military labour market;
those traditions were being adopted to British imperial
preferences. The recruitment system for example,
endorsed the traditional British preference for peasants as
best potential recruits and followed the colonial
stereotypes that wheat-eating groups were physically
more suitable for the job, although such ethnic
stereotyping became a much more important factor in
army recruitment in the late nineteenth century rather
than in the eighteenth. During the initial formative phase,
Hastings did not want to disturb the existing caste rules
in the affairs of the army. So the Company's army
consisted mainly of upper caste Brahman and Rajput
landed peasants from Awadh and the Rajput and
Bhumihar Brahman peasants from north and south Bihar-
both wheat-eating regions. These people joined the
Company's army because the pay, allowances, pension
and resettlement provisions offered by the Company
were much better than those offered by the regional
States and what was most important, salaries were paid
regularly. The deliberate policy of respecting caste,
dietary, travel and others religious practices of the
Sepoys fostered a high caste identity of the Company's
army. By joining it many of the upcoming socially
ambitious castes like the Bhumihar-Brahmans could
fulfill their aspirations for social mobility. Cornwallis,
despite his preference for Anglicisation, did not disturb
this specific organization of the army, and as a result, the
Company came to possess a high caste army, which was
prone to revolt when their social privileges and pecuniary
benefits were cut from the 1820s. As the Company's
territories expanded to the west beyond the Bengal
frontiers into the mountainous Jungle Terai, in the 1770s
and then into the Ceded and Conquered Districts in 1802
there was another attempt to recruit from among the hill
tribes. While in the plains the Company ran permanent
recruitment centres, in the hills recruitment was made
through local notables and payment was offered through
the Mughal system of ghatwali service tenures. The defeat
of the Indian States, particularly of Mysore in the late
eighteenth and of the Marathas in the early in nineteenth
centuries created another vast reservoir of surplus armed
manpower to recruit from; but the Company's army could
not absorb all the disbanded soldiers of the Indian princes.
Then from 1815 there was another experiment to recruit
Gurkha soldiers from among the Nepalis, Garwahlis and
Sirmouli hill men. A skilful blending of the Nepali martial
tradition and European training and discipline made the
Gurkhas the most trusted soldiers in the British army.

:

questions.optionC: Eight guilds of people below the Sudras

According to Al-Beruni the antyajas were
Eight guilds of people below the sudras.

Antyaja : Alberuni lists eight Antyaja castes below
the status of the sudras.

castes but outside them.

Balban established a separate army department
"Diwan-i-arz" to fight with Mongols.

questions.explanation:

Tughlaq built a Khankah for him where he taught and

open. The formal gateway to the iwan is called pishtaq,

building, usually decorated with calligraphy bonds
glazed tileworks and geometric designs.

was
questions.explanation:
The founder of the Nizam's State in
Hyderabad was Chin Kilich Khan. Kilich Khan
disgusted with the Mughal emperor who had appointed
Mubariz Khan as a full fledged Viceroy of Deccan,
decided to fight Mubariz Khan. He defeated and Later
killed Mubariz Khan in the Battle of Shakr-i-Kheda
(1724). He now assumed the control of Deccan in 1725.

Asaf Jah.

responsibility for education of masses.

for higher studies and vernacular at school level.

Read the following passage and answer the questions
numbers 71 to 75:
Asoka (c. 273-236 B.C.), the grandson of Chandragupta,
styled 'the beloved of the gods' and 'of lovable
appearance', succeeded to the throne of Pataliputra by
winning a fratricidal war. Nine years after his accession
he rounded off the empire which he inherited from his
grandfather by annexing Kalinga. The Kalinga war
brought to the emperor a violent reaction, no doubt under
the influence of Buddha's teachings. He regretted the vast
numbers of men killed or taken prisoner; he bemoaned
the lot of pious men and women to whom befell 'personal
violence, death or banishment from loved ones'; and he
eschewed for ever war as an instrument of governance.
'If any one does him wrong, the "beloved of the god"
must bear all that can be borne. He embarked on a career
of Dharma Vijaya, conquest through Dharma. He set up
a network of missions to preach Dharma; declared that
all men were his children; 'and what little effort I make, -
what is it for ? - (in order) that I may be free from debt to
the creatures, that I may render some happy here and that
they may gain heaven in the next world', said he. The
Emperor constituted himself as the guardian of the moral
and material welfare of the world.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History June 2014 Paper III
questions.questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and choose the
correct answer of the questions that follow (Q. No. 1
to 5):
In the middle of the fourth century of the Christian era,
something resembling a volcanic eruption took place in
the history of the human race. The Hunas, like a varitable
stream of lava, issued from their homeland on the
northern shores of the Caspian Sea and spread over
Europe and Asia. Homeless and lawless, they rode their
horses awake and asleep. Their fierce yells spread terror
wherever they were heard. They engaged all the civilized
peoples of the world in fearful cataclysmic wars and
wherever they could, they killed, destroyed, burnt and
devastated with demoniac ruthlessness. In Europe, Attila
the Hun brought about the downfall of even the powerful
Roman Empire.
About A.D. 455, the Hunas began to enter India.
Emperor Skanda-gupta drove them back by a supreme
effort. Twelve years later, he died. The outposts of the
empire, already weak, could offer no further resistance.
The barbarian hordes, after passing through Persia and
destroying the Kushana rulers of the north-west, began to
pour into India. A war of succession appears to have
followed the death of Skanda-gupta, weakening the
empire in the hour of its danger. Next in order of
succession, five emperors including Narasimha-gupta
baladitya, between A.D. 500 and 570, held precarious
sway over parts of the empire, which in spite of its
decadence was still a name to conjure with. Many parts
of the empire outside the bounds of the compact core of
the empire became independent. In Saurashtra, a
province of the empire, the Maitraka general practically
threw off his allegiance on the death of Skanda-gupta.
By A.D. 512, the Hunas under Toramana, overran north
India up to Eran in the Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh.
Toramana's son, Mihirakula, a veritable terror, spread
fire and carnage from the Punjab to Gwalior and by A.D.
525 became the master of a vast territory. Northern India
soon recovered from the shock of the barbarian impact
and resisted Mihirakula.

weakened after the death of Skanda Gupta.

The local governors became independent after
the death of Skanda Gupta.

exercised just titular control after the death of
Skanda Gupta.

The death of Skanda Gupta coincided with
the death of the Gupta empire.

the Gupta power by defeating his enemies, who may
have been rebels or foreign invadors. He repulsed the
invasion of Indo Hephthalites (known as Hunas in
India.
Skandagupta issued five type of gold coins–
1. Archer type
2. King and queen type
3. Chhatra type
4. Lion slayer type
5. Horseman type
Skandagupta issued four type of silver coins–
1. Garuda type
2. Bull type
3. Altar type
4. Madhyadesha type

cheramal.

27. Consider the following statements about the
agrarian system under the Delhi Sultanate and
Mughal Empire:

1. Alauddin Khilji imposed taxes called Charai
and Ghari.

2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq imposed additional
cesses called abwabs on the peasants.

3. Under Akbar, Zabt system of land revenue
assessment was further developed and it came
to be called Dahsala system.

4. Jahangir introduced the Nasq system of
assessment.

Which of the statements given above is/are
correct? Select your answer from the
questions.explanation:
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are true about the
agrarian system under the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal
Empire.
1. Alauddin Khilji imposed taxes called Charai (taxes
on grazing) and Ghari (tax on residence).
2. Muhammad bin Tughlaq imposed additional cesses
called abwabs on the peasants.
3. Under Akbar, Zabt system of land revenue
assessment was further developed and it came to be
called Dahsala system.
 Nasq system of assessment was introduced by Akbar
in the area from Lahore to Allahabad and in Malwa and
Gujarat.

Direction: Read the given paragraph and answer the
questions given below Q.N. 47 to Q.N. 50.
There is an interesting case of prohibition of drinking
wine. The Sultan personally gave up drinking. The royal
drinking vessels of glass and porcelain were broken
before the Badaun Gate, and wine from the royal jars
was poured out, creating mud and mire as in the rainy
season. Then officers mounted on elephants proclaimed
in the streets and lanes of Delhi that no one was to drink
or sell liquor or go near it. The licensed tavern-keepers
and distillers of liquor were driven out of Delhi and the
revenue from them was written off. Persons with self
respect gave up drinking at the first warning. But others
distilled liquor from sugar in their houses and sold it at a
high price, they also tried to get jars of liquor from out
side the city hidden in carts under wood and grass. Sultan
Alauddin ordered dry wells to be dug near the Badaun
Gate, and persons who were found disobeying his order.
Were thrown into them; most of them died, and those
who survived regained their health only after prolonged
treatment. It was possible at the worst of times to go ten
or twelve karohs out of Delhi for a good drink. But no
drink was available within four or five karohs of Delhi in
suburbs like Ghiyaspur, Indrapat and Kailugarhi.
Ultimately, sultan relented and passed an order that if a
man distilled liquor in his own house for his own
consumption but was not guilty of selling it or of calling
a drinking party, he was not to be molested and the spies
were not to enter his house.

Babur (founder of Mughal empire). It is written in
Turki. During reign of Akbar Baburnama completely
translated to Persian by a Mughal Courtier Abdul
Rahim in (1589-90).

Ded as his spiritual preceptor?

spiritual preceptor.

Shaivism Philosophy. She was the creator of the style

questions.explanation:

Turkan-i-Chihalgani?
questions.explanation:
Turkan-i-Chahalgani was the council of 40
turkic and non turkic slave Amirs who administered the
Delhi Sultanate as per the wishes of Sultan. It was
founded by Iltutmish. Bahauddin Tughril, Qutlugh
Khan, Balban etc. were the member of Chahalgani
Balban destroyed 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani, because they
started interfering in Administration and they tried to
deny the power of king.

against women being considered as inferior to
men in her work Hadibadeya Dharma (tenets
for chaste and devoted wives) :

Sanchi Honamma was a poetess in the court

language.
She

women
being
considered as inferior to men.

Mughals is attributed to Bidar Architectural style. Bidar
was a port of Bahmanid kingdom. Bahmani kingdom
Broke down in five parts :

(2) Ahmednagar

(4) Berar

upon by Jahangir as Gardabad (city of dust)
and Jahannamabad (city of hell)?
questions.explanation:
When Jahangir, Akbar's son-first visited
Ahmedabad in 1617 A.D. He did not like the place and
called it Gardabad (city of dust) and Jahannamabad
(City of hell).

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II
questions.questionText:
34. Mughal emperors used to confer various types
of standards upon nobles. Which of the
following was added in the list of standards by
Shahjahan?
questions.explanation:
The Mahi Maratib was the highest honour
in the Mughal empire. It symbolized honour bravery
and strength and the Mughal emperors only conferred it
upon their highest dignitaries. It comprise giant face of
Rohu Fish with scales and iron teeth mounted on a
large pole. This honour of Mahi Maratib was instituted
by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan around 1632 C.E.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II
questions.questionText:

signed by the British with Native States and
select the correct answer code :

(A) The Treaty of Salbai

(B) The Treaty of Bassien (Vasai)

(C) The Treaty of Srirangapattanam

(D) The Treaty of Allahabad and Kara
questions.explanation:
(d) Treaty of Allahabad and Kara (1765) was signed
between Mughal emperor Shah Alam II and East
India Company after Battle of Buxar.
(a) Treaty of Salbai was signed by representatives of
Maratha empire and East India Company in 1802.
(c) Treaty of Seringpatnam (1792) was signed between
Nizam + Maratha + East India Company and
Tipu Sultan.
(d) Treaty of Bassein was signed between Peshwa
Bajirao II and East India Company.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II

ignorance I hold every man a traitor who,
while educated at their expense, pays not the
least heed to them."
questions.explanation:
Following words were said by Swami
Vivekananda. Swami Vivekananda was born in 1862.
He was disciple of Ram Krishna Paramhansa. His
mission was to bridge the gulf between Paramaratha
(Service) and Vyavahara (behaviour) and between
spirituality and day to day life. He believed in the
fundamental oneness of God.

Union Congress?
questions.explanation:
The All India Trade Union Congress
(AITUC) is the Oldest Trade Union Federation in
India. It was founded on 31 October, 1920 with Lala
Lajpat Rai as its first president.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II
questions.questionText:
40. Who among the following Viceroys made the
'August Offer' to secure Indian Co-operation in
the war effort?
questions.explanation:
The August offer was an offer made by
Viceroy Linlithgow in 1940 promising the expansion
of the executive council of viceroy of India to include
more Indians, the establishment of an advisory council
giving full weight to minority opinion and the
recognition of Indians right to frame their own
constitution.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II

Revolution
technology
for
agricultural
development?
questions.explanation:
India adopted Green revolution technology
for agricultural development from U.S.A. Green
revolution in India was led by Agricultural Scientist
M.S. Swaminathan under Prime ministership of
congress leader Lal Bahadur Shastri and the green
revolution within India commenced in 1966, leading to
increase in food grain production.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II
questions.questionText: 42. The doctrine 'The sons of the soil' is related to:
questions.explanation:
The "Sons of the Soil" doctrine underlies the
view that a state specifically belongs to the main
linguistic group inhabiting it. All others who lived there
and whose mother tongue is not state's main language
are declared 'outsiders'.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper II

questions.explanation:
Thomas Paine was on English born American
political activist philosopher and revolutionary. He
authored "Common Sense" (1776) and American
crisis (1776-1783). The two most influential pamphlets
at the start of American revolution. He also authored
"Rights of man" book.

questions.explanation:

between the present and the past"?
questions.explanation:
Edward Holett Carr (English historian

history" as an unending dialogue between the present
and past. So option (c) is correct answer.

Determining the significance of historical data etc.

[(i), (iv), (ii), (iii)]
(i)
Arrian (60 BCE - 86 BCE) – Greek historian
composed 'Anabasis of Alexander'.
(iv) Strabo (63 BC - 23 AD) – Composed
"Geographica"
(ii)
Pliny (23/24 AD - 79 AD) – Roman Author
wrote the encyclopedic "Naturalis Historika"
(iii) Ptolemy (100 AD - 170 AD)

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
11. The cultural sequence of the excavated site of
Hastinapur from bottom upwards is as under :

(i) Kushan period

(ii) N.B.P. ware period

(iii) O.C.P. period

(iv) P.G.W. period
questions.explanation:
[(iii), (iv), (ii), (i)]
(iii)
Ochured Colour pottery belong to Harappan
period.
(iv)
Painted grey ware culture associated with Early
Vedic period.
(ii)
North Black Polished ware culture associated
with Later Vedic period.
(i)
Kushan period comes in last.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
12. Arrange the following authors of inscriptions in
the chronological order :

(i) Harisena

(ii) Ravikirti

(iii) Vatsabhatti

(iv) Virasena
questions.explanation:
[(i), (iii), (iv), (ii)]
(i)
Harisena was court poet of king Samudragupta
and inscribed Prayag Prashasti in 4th century
BCE.
(iii) Vatsa Bhatti inscribed "Mandsaur Inscription"
in 473 BCE.
(iv) Virasena inscribed 'Udaigiri Inscription' in the
kingship
of
Chandragupta
II,
son
of
Samudragupta.
(ii)
Ravikirti (7th century BCE) Inscribed Aihole
Inscription. He was court poet of Pulkeshin II.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
13. Which were the chief ports of the Pandyas of
the Sangam age ? Select the correct answer
from the code given below :

(i) Korkhai

(ii) Madurai

(iii) Musiri

(iv) Puhar
questions.explanation:
[(i) and (ii)]
Korkhai and Madurai were the chief ports of pandyas of
the Sangam age.
 Puhar was the port of Cholas.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
14. According to inscriptional assertions who
among the following rulers used to honour all
religions?

(i) Asoka

(ii) Kanishka

(iii) Kharavela

(iv) Pushyamitra Sunga
questions.explanation:
[(i) and (iii)]
According to inscriptional assertions Ashoka and
Kharvela rulers used to honour all religions.
Although Ashoka follow the Buddhism but he honoured
all religions.
Hathigumpha inscription describes Kharvela as a
devotee of all religions.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
15. Consider the following statements :

Assertion (A) : Immediately after his accession
to
the
throne,
Maharaja
Kharavela launched on a career
of a Digvijayin (conqueror).
Reason (R) : Having heard about the exploits
of Kharavela, Dimita an Indo-
Greek King of Eastern Punjab,
retreated
to
Mathura
from
where he planned to challenge
Kharavela.

In the context of the above statements, which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
[(A) is true but (R) is false]
Assertion - Immediately after his accession to the
throne, Kharvela launched a career of a Digvijayin is
correct.
but Reason - Having heard about the exploits of
Kharvela, Dimita an Indogreek king of eastern Punjab,
retreated to Mathura from where he planned to
challenge Kharvela is not correct.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
16. Who among the following kings had performed
the Vajapeya sacrifice ?

(i) Pravarasena I

(ii) Pushyamitra Sunga

(iii) Santamula I

(iv) Satakarni Gautamiputra
questions.explanation:
[(i) and (iii) only]
Pravarsena I and Santamula I performed Vajapeya
sacrifice.
 Vajapeya sacrifice is vedic yajnas which is mentioned
in Yajurveda. This sacrifice was organised to show
Valour and amuse the subjects (praja). Subjects enjoyed
chariot race in this sacrifice.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
17. Amravati, an early historical site in Andhra
Pradesh was known as the following :
questions.explanation:
Dharnikota
Amaravati formerly known as Dharnikota is an
important city which glorifies the cultural Heritage and
history of Andhra Pradesh. It was the capital of
Satavahana dynasty of the Andhra. The city was also
once a Holy site of Mahayana Buddhism. The city used
to have a large Buddhist Stupa known as Mahachaitra.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
18. Consider the following statements :

Assertion (A) : The foremost success of the
Gupta emperor Chandragupta
II was his victory over the
mighty Saka-Kshatrapa dynasty
of Gujarat.
Reason (R) : It could have given the Guptas
access to Indian trade with the
Mediteranean.

In the context of the above statements, which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation (A).
questions.explanation:
[Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct
explanation of (A)]
The foremost success of Gupta emperor Chandragupta
II was his victory over the mighty Saka- Kshatrapa
dynasty of Gujarat because it could have given the
Guptas access to Indian trade with Mediterranean.
Hence option (a) is correct answer.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
19. The Hunas issued coins only in

(i) Gold

(ii) Silver

(iii) Copper

(iv) Potin
questions.explanation:
[(ii) and (iii) only]
The coins of Hunas include the gold and silver coins
those were finally executed and bare the name is
Pahlavi and Which were read as Napki Neski or
Nazeki. Some of the coins also had the title of Maleka
(that means king).

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
20. Arrange the following astronomers in the
chronological order :

(i) Aryabhata II

(ii) Bhaskaracharya

(iii) Bhattotpala

(iv) Brahmagupta
questions.explanation:
[(iv), (i), (ii), (iii)]
Brahmagupta (598 CE - 668 CE)
Aryabhatta (476 AD - 550 AD)
Bhaskaracharya (1114 AD - 1185 AD)
Bhattotpala (10th century)

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
21. Which of the following temples are built of
bricks ?

(i) Begram temple of Dinajpur

(ii) Sat Deuliya of Burdwan, W.B.

(iii) Sidhesvara of Bahulara, Bankura, W.B.

(iv) Vaital Deul of Bhuvanesvara
questions.explanation:
[(i), (ii) and (iii)]
Baigram temple of Dinajpur, Sat Deuliya of Burdwan
W.B. and Siddheswara of Bahulara, Banka, W.B. are
temple built of Bricks.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
22. The Vimala temple of Dilwara is dedicated to
one of the following :
questions.explanation:
Adinatha
The Vimala temple of Dilwara is dedicated to
Adinatha.
Dilwara temples are a group of Svetambara Jain
temples in Rajasthan. The Earliest were built by Vimal
Shah and supposedly designed or at least financed by
Vastupala, Jain minister of Dholka. They dated
between the 11th and 16th centuries forming some of
the most famous monuments in the style of Maru-
Gurjara Architecture famous for their use of a very pure
white marble and intricate marble carving.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
23. The Lakshmi type coins of Gangeyadeva
Kalchuri were imitated by which of the
following rulers ?

(i) Bhoja II Pratihara

(ii) Govindachandra Gahadvala

(iii) Parmardideva Chandella

(iv) Udayaditya Paramara
questions.explanation:
[(ii), (iii) and (iv)]
The Lakshmi type coins of Gangeyadeva kalchuri were
Imitated by Govind Chandra Gahadavala, Parmardideva
Chandella and Udayaditya Paramara.
 Muhammad Ghori also minted Lakshmi coins. After
defeating Prithviraj in second battle of Tarain Ghori
minted coins that were almost Identical to Prithviraj
coins.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
24. Who among the following rulers of Kashmir
built a dam on Vitasta river to save his
Kingdom from the devastating floods ?
questions.explanation:
Avantivarman
Avantivarman of Kashmir built a dam on Vitasta river
to save his kingdom from devastating floods.
 Avantivarman was a king who founded the Utpala
dynasty. He ruled Kashmir from 855 to 883 CE and
built the Avantiswami temple.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
25. Consider the following statements :

Assertion (A) : The 12th century unique work
Kumarapalacharita
by
Hemachandra is a long poem
which
tells
the
story
of
Chaulukya Kings of Gujarat.
Reason (R) : It
illustrates
the
rules
of
Sanskrit and Prakrit Grammar
also.

In the context of the above statements, which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
[Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct
explanation of (A)]
Kumarapala
Charita
was
composed
by
Hemachandra between 1089-1173 AD. This book is
divided in 20 parts (Sargas). This book was vivid
description about Chalukya dynasty. First Twelve
Sargas composed in Sanskrit and last eight sargas
composed in prakrat. This book is also called "Dvaya
Shraya". Hence option (a) is correct answer.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
26. Which one of the following pairs is not matched
correctly ?
questions.explanation:
Al Ghazali-Tahzib al-Akhlaq
4th pair is not correctly matched because Tahzib al
Akhlaq is related to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
(1) Shihabuddin Suhrawardi – Awarif-ul Ma'arif
(2) Al-Hujwiri
– Kashf-ul Mahjub
(3) Ibn-al Arabi
– Fusus al-Hikam

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
27. "I and none other." "What are you that I am
not and what have you been that I have not
been."

The above statement was claimed by which of
the following group/Sultan ?
questions.explanation:
Turkan-i-Chihalgani
"I and none other". "What are you that I am not and
what have you been that I have not been", this statement
was claimed by Turkan-i-Chihalgani.
Turkan-i-Chihalgani was group of 40 Amirs created
by Iltutmish. Balban was also member of this group
and Balban destroyed this group.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
28. Which of the following statements are not
correct in regard of music ?

(i) Barani writes about young girls being trained
by Indian courtesans in Persian and Indian
music for the Delhi Court in the late
thirteenth century.

(ii) Amir Khusrau in 1318 claimed that Indian
music had pre-eminence over the music of all
other countries.

(iii) Abul Fazl does not include the names of
musicians in the Ain-i Akbari.

(iv) Nayak Bakhshu was the recognized master of
khayal.
questions.explanation:
[(iii) and (iv)]
Statement (iii) and (iv) are not correct about music.
(iii)
Abul Fazl does not include the names of
musician in Ain-i-Akbari.
(iv)
Nayak Bakhshu was the recognised master of
Khayal.

Abul Fazl mentioned 'Tansen' as musician in
Ain-i-Akbari.

Amir Khusrau invented 'Khayal' and he was
master of Khayal & Qawwali.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
29. What arguments did Miyan Bhuwah give for
writing Madanush Shifa-i Sikandarshahi, a
compilation based on all the major Ayurvedic
texts in Sanskrit ?

(i) The Greek medicine did not suit the climate
of India.

(ii) The medicinal plants mentioned in the Greek
system
were
either
unidentifiable
or
unobtainable in India.

(iii) The Greek school of medicine became
dominant at the Delhi Court.

(iv) Grecco-Arabic tradition was identical in its
practices.
questions.explanation:
[(i) and (ii)]
Miya Bhuwah gave following arguments for writing
Madnush shifa-i-Sikandarshahi compilation based on
all the major Ayurvedic texts in Sanskrit.
(i)
The Greek medicine did not suit the climate of
India.
(ii) The medicinal plants mentioned in the greek
system were either unidentifiable or unobtainable
in India.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
30. Which one of the following is not true about the
Saiyid and Lodi architecture ?
questions.optionA:
Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul's tomb inspired the
Saiyid and Lodi rulers to build octagonal
tombs.
questions.optionB:
The inner and outer shell of the dome, with a
space left between the two in Sikandar's
tomb, marks the beginning of the double
dome.
questions.optionC:
Saiyids and Lodi's did not erect any square-
plan tombs.
questions.optionD:
The Sur family tombs at Sasaram are all
octagonal.
questions.explanation:
Saiyids and Lodi's did not erect any square
plan tombs.

Most of the Sayyids and Lodi's tomb were in
octagonal style. The attempts in the direction of double
dome started with tomb of Taj Khan and tomb of
Sikandar Lodi. However the fully mature form of the
double dome is seen first time in India in the tomb of
Humayun.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
31. Match List-I with List-II and select the correct
answer with the help of the code given below :

List-I
List-II

(A) Qalb
i. Cavalry Trooper

(B) Hashm ii. Enhancement in the estimated

income of the iqta.

(C) Fawazil iii. Army

(D) Taufir iv. Excess revenue over and above

the - assigned revenue
questions.explanation:
[A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii)]
(A) Qalb
– Army
(B) Hashm
– Cavalry Trooper
(C) Fawazil
– Excess revenue over and above the
assigned revenue.
(D) Taufir
– Enhancement in the estimated income
of Iqta.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
32. "As the wind destroys the trees, and locusts the
Shali crop, so did the Yavanas destroy the
usages of Kashmira ..... the Kingdom of
Kashmira was polluted by the evil practices of
the Mlecchhas."

The above statement about Kashmir was made
by which of the following chroniclers of
Kashmir ?
questions.explanation:
Jonaraja
The statement "As the wind destroys the trees and
locusts the shali crop, so did the Yavanas destroy the
usages of Kashmira ....... the Kingdom of Kashmira was
polluted by the evil practices of the Mlecchhas". was
given by Jonaraja.
 Jonaraja was Kashmiri historian in the court of king
Jainul Abidin. He wrote Dvitiya Rajatarangini
continuation of Kalhana's Rajatarangini and which
brings chronicle of the kings of Kashmir down to the
time of Zainul Abidin. In his Dvitiya Rajatarangini
he has vividly described the decline of the Hindu ruling
dynasty and rise of Muslim ruling dynasty in Kashmir.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText: 33. Which one of the following is not correct ?
questions.optionA:
The Pichola lake of Udaipur was excavated
during Lakha's rule (1382-1421) on Mewar.
questions.optionB:
Mokal (1421-33) repaired the temples of
Samidheshwara at Chittor.
questions.optionC:
Rana Kumbha (1433-68) dug several lakes
for irrigation purposes as well as step- wells
and reservoirs for storing water.
questions.optionD:
Rana Uda (1468-73) constructed Udai Sagar
Lake in Udaipur.
questions.explanation:
Statement (d), Rana Uda constructed
Udaisagar lake in Udaipur is not correct Udai Sagar
Lake is situated in Udaipur. This lake was built by
Maharana Udai Singh in 1565. Udai Sagar Lake is
around 4 km in length 2.5 km in width and 9 meters
deep at maximum, it is fed by the Ahar river.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
34. "Suha Bhatt strove hard so that the Sultan at
his suggestion ordered all Brahmans and
learned Hindus should become Musalmans and
those who did not accept Islam should leave the
realm."

In the above statement reference is made to
which of the following Sultan by Ferishta ?
questions.explanation:
Sultan Sikandar of Kashmir
"Suha Bhatta strove hard so that the sultan at his
suggestion ordered all Brahmans and learned Hindus
should become musalman and those who did not accept
Islam should leave the realm". In this statement
Ferishta made reference about Sultan Sikandar of
Kashmir.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
35. Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason
(R) :

Assertion (A) : Bengal Sultan Ruknuddin
Barbak Shah I was a great
patron of Bengali literature.
Reason (R) : Barbak Shah I conferred the
title
of
Gunaraj
Khan
to
Maladhar
Basu
in
acknowledgement of his great
achievements in the field of
Bengali literature.

In the context of the above statements which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation (A).
questions.explanation:
Both (A) and (R) true and (R) is correct
explanation of (A)
Barbak Shah I Sultan of Bengal was patron of Bengali
literature for the poem in early Bangla of Maladhar
Basu in which he focuses on divine life of Krishna,
honoured with the title "Gunaraj Khan" by Rukunuddin
Barbak Shah. So option (a) is correct answer.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
36. Match List-I with List-II relating to the
organisation of the Sikh Community and
choose correct answer from the code given
below ?

List-I
List-II

(A) Masand i. Persons initiated by the Guru

himself

(B) Khalsa ii. Representative of the Guru

(C) Meli
iii. Persons initiated by the Masand

(D) Sahlang iv. Deputies of the Masand
questions.explanation:
[A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(iii)]
(a) Masand
– Representative of Guru
(b) Khalsa
– Persons initiated by the Guru

himself
(c) Meli
– Deputies of Masand
(d) Sahlang
– persons initiated by the Masand.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
37. Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason
(R) :

Assertion (A) : Eknath has written his Hindu-
Turk Samvad in Bharud genre.
Reason (R) : The Bharuds were specially
written to appeal to masses, to
interest those who otherwise
might not listen to the message
of Bhakti.

In the context of the above statements which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct
explanation of (A).
Bharud is very old poetic form mainly used by the
Saint poets like Eknath. This poet is credited with
writing 300 Bharuds on 125 subjects. Bharud is double
meaning Marathi dramatic song. Under the guise of
comedy, it condemned various inhuman practices
prevalent in different cults. Bharud also helps in
exposing silly customs. Hence option (a) is correct
answer.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
38. Mahdawis asserted on the purification of
historical Islam from innovation (bida). Which
one of the following views of the scholars is not
correct ?
questions.optionA:
Mohammad Yasin has characterised the
movement as 'a plebian revolt of the simple-
hearted'.
questions.optionB:
K. A. Nizami refers to Mahdawi movement as
'a crisis and a connotation in the lower strata'.
questions.optionC:
Derry MacLean argues that the early
Mahdawis tended to prefer a low profile and a
quietist stance; while the later Mahadawis
generally adopted an uncompromising stance.
questions.optionD:
A.S.B. Ansari has compared the Mahdawi
'Cult of the digger' to the 'Ismaili Assassins'.
questions.explanation:
Mahadawis asserted on the purification of
historical Islam from innovation (Bida) views of Derry
MacLean is not correct "Derry MacLean Argues that
the early Mahadawis tended to prefer a low profile and
a quietist stance; while later Mahadawis generally
adopted an uncompromising stance.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
39. Consider the following statements concerning
the Mughal Zamindars :

(i) Zamindar holding a full Pargana had to
render military service with a fixed
contingent.

(ii) Zamindar holding only a part (taraf) of a
few villages in a Pargana paid Salami.

(iii) One half of the Zamindar's territory whose
revenue zamindars were to deposit in the
state treasury was known as talpad.

Select the correct answer from the codes given
below :
questions.explanation:
[(i) and (ii)]
Statement (i) and (ii) are true regarding Mughal
Zamindari System.
(i) Zamindar holding a full pargana had to render
military services with definite troops.
(ii) Zamindar holding a part (Taraf) of a few villages in
a Pargana paid Salami.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
40. A large number of marks and symbols,
sometimes accompanied by the names of
individuals, are found inscribed on almost all
the stones used in the construction of medieval
monuments.

These marks and symbols carried some
purpose. Which of the following purpose is not
relevant in regard of inscribing the marks ?
questions.optionB:
Inscribed mark should be exclusive of a
creator.
questions.optionC: Stone supplier or mason used the mark.
questions.optionD:
To identify a building and the owner of a
building.
questions.explanation:
to identify a building and the owner of a
building
Purpose of inscribing large number of marks and
symbols on medieval monuments was not to identify a
building and the owner of a building.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
41. Which one of the following European travellers
commented "in India, there were no academies
(except Madrasas for religious study) where
systematic study of the western sciences could
be taken up. Thus interest in western science
and philosophy was individual and died with
the individual" ?
questions.explanation:
Bernier
The statement "In India, there were no academies where
systematic study of the western sciences could be taken
up. Thus interest in western science and philosophy was
individual and died with individual" is given by
Bernier.
 Bernier was a French physician. He stayed 12 years
in India. He came India in Aurangzeb’s ruling period.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
42. Which one of the following statements is not
correct in regard to painting ?
questions.optionA:
The Mughal emperor Humayun brought
master painters - Abdu's Samad and Mir
Saiyid Ali from Persia in 1555.
questions.optionB:
Akbar established a large atelier that
undertook the Hamzanama in the 1560s.
questions.optionC:
Jahangir's period rejected the European
influence on the painting.
questions.optionD:
In the 18th century, regional paintings came
into existence, depicting especially Krishna
Lilas.
questions.explanation:
Jahangir's period rejected the European
influence on the painting
The influence of European art has ever seen in the
Jahangir's period also. Europeans introduced the art of
pietradura divinity concept in Mughal paintings.
Three dimensional techniques, foreshortening. So
option (c) is correct answer.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
43. Given below are two statements, one labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason
(R) :

Assertion (A) : Kos minar is a category of
architecture that developed with
a clear association with road
networks.
Reason (R) : Minar's primary function was to
serve as markers of following
correct
route
for
their
destination.

In the context of the above statements which of
the following is correct ?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the
correct explanation (A).
questions.explanation:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct
explanation of (A)
The Kos Minars are medieval Indian milestones along
the
Grand
Trunk
road
in
Northern
Indian
Subcontinent that were introduced by 16th century
pashtun ruler Shershah Suri. Kos Minars were erected
to serve as markers of distance along Royal routes from
Agra to Ajmer, Agra to Lahore and from Agra to
Mandu. Hence option (a) is correct answer.

B.H.

W.H. Wiser opined that village servants and

not correct in relation to village community. So option

reimposition of Jizya by Aurangazeb ?

Jizya was levied on account of the opposition
of the Hindus and the greed of the rulers.

Jizya was imposed by aurangazeb for he

Islam.

pressure on the general treasury.

Jizya was reimposed by Aurangzeb in 1679.

49. Which of the following are correct explanation
in regard of Maratha interest to support the
Mughal emperor against the invasion of Nadir
Shah ?

(i) Marathas considered Nadir Shah's invasion as
intrusion by an outsider.

(ii) If Nadir Shah was to stay in India and found a
new dynasty, it would be a big blow against
Maratha ambition.

(iii) Shahu instructed Baji Rao to hurry to the aid
of
the
Emperor
in
accordance
with
understanding to Aurangazeb that whenever
the Empire was in any difficulty, Marathas
would help.

(iv) Bajirao immediately rushed to help the
Mughal army.
questions.explanation:
[(i), (ii) and (iii)]
Marathas helped Mughal emperor against Nadir Shah.
(i)
Maratha considered Nadir Shah's invasion as
intrusion by an outsider.
(ii) If nadir Shah was to stay in India, found a new
dynasty, it would be a big blow against Maratha
ambition.
(iii) Shahu instructed Bajirao to hurry to aid of the
emperor in accordance with understanding to
Aurangzeb that whenever the empire was in
difficulty Marathas would help.

questions.questionText:

Mohan Roy) labours, to our mind, seems to lie
in his fight against the forces of medievalism in
India, and it is for this reason, that we claim for
him the honour of being the father of the
present Indian Renaissance."

Who wrote these words ?
questions.explanation:
Bipin Chandra pal
A famous extremist leader Bipin Chandra Pal stated.
"The chief value of Raja's (Raja Ram Mohan Roy)
labours, to our mind, seems to lie in his fight against the
forces of medievalism in India and it is for this reason,
that we claim for him the honour of being the father of
the present Indian Renaissance.

Rawalpindi ?

Dec. 1856
The first female school was opened at Rawalpindi under
the Auspices of Mr. Browne, inspector of schools, in
December 1856. By the close of year 1856-57.

questions.questionText:
55. The Vernacular Press Act IX of 1878 became
law on March 14 and it was operative in all the
provinces, except Madras because
questions.optionA: Natives of Madras were pro British.
questions.optionB:
Madras province had only English papers
during that time.
questions.optionC:
Here the press in Indian languages was not
yet strong.
questions.optionD:
In Madras most of the vernacular printing
presses were owned by the British.
questions.explanation:
Here the press in Indian languages was not
yet strong.
Vernacular Press Act 1878 designed to 'better control'
the vernacular press and effectivelly punish and repress
seditious writing. Vernacular Press Act 1878 passed in
the Viceroyship of Lytton.
This act was nick named "the gagging act ".

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
56. In 1884-88, a twenty two year old Hindu
woman was taken to Bombay High Court by
her husband; what is the name of this case ?
questions.explanation:
Rukhmabai - Dadaji Case
In 1884, Rukhmabai, a 22 years old Hindu woman was
taken to Bombay High Court by her husband Bhikaji
after she refused to live with him, after this case in 19
March, 1891, Age of Consent Act was passed by
government of Lord Lansdowne raising the age of
consent for consummation from ten to twelve year.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
57. In which year the very famous book 'Stree-
Purush Tulana' (A comparison between women
and men) of Tarabai Shinde was published ?
questions.explanation:
1882
'Stree-Purush Tulana' of Tarabai Sinde was published
in 1882, this text is in Marathi. This literary work is
critique of upper caste patriarchy and the gender and
caste system in 19th century India. The material is also
considered the first modern feminist text of India.
Shinde questions the position of women in the society.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
58. In which year was Indian National Social
Conference Session separated from the session
of Indian National Congress ?
questions.explanation:
1895
In 1895 Indian National Social Conference Session was
separated from the session of Indian National Congress.
 Indian National Social Conference was founded
by M.G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao. It was virtually
the social reform cell of the Indian National Congress.
Its first session was held in Madras in December 1887.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III

of 'the safety volve theory' regarding the origin
of Indian National Congress ?
questions.explanation:
C.F. Andrews and Girija Mukherji accepted
The myth of the safety volve theory.
Lala Lajpat Rai used the "Safety Volve" theory in
"Young India" in 1916 and said that it was a product of
brain of Lord Dufferin.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
64. In which year did Swami Shraddhanand
started Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar ?
questions.explanation:
1902
Swami Shraddhanand started Gurukul Kangri at
Haridwar in 1902. Swami Shraddhanand was an Indian
Independence activist and Arya Samaj Sannyasi. He
played a key role in Sangathan (consolidation) and
organisation) and Suddhi (Purification), a Hindu reform
in 1920s.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
65. In which year Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
were deported ?
questions.explanation:
1907
Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh deported in 1907. The
colonisation Bill passed in 1906 and the bill provided
for transfer of property of a person after his death to the
government if he had no heirs. So agitation started in
Punjab. Agitation was led by Ajit Singh. During this
agitation Ajit Singh founded secret society "Anjuman-i
Muhiban-i-Watan".
This
agitation
ended
with
deportation of Ajit Singh and Lala lajpat Rai.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
66. Whom among the following published in 1908
first regular propaganda sheet, 'The Free
Hindustan' in U.S.A. ?
questions.explanation:
Taraknath Das
Taraknath Das, who was a student published a
magazine "Free Hindustan" in 1908 in Seattle
advocating armed rebellion against the British rule and
P.S. Khamkhoje who went to USA in 1907 established
the Indian Independence league.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
67. Who said, "A government is an instrument of
service only in so far as it is based upon the will
and consent of people. It is an instrument of
oppression where it enforces submission by
coercion. Oppression, therefore, ceases when
people cease to fear terror - of law or arms" ?
questions.explanation:
Mahatma Gandhi
The statement "A government is an instrument of
service only in so far as it is based upon the will and
consent of people. It is an instrument of oppression
where it enforces submission by coercion. Oppression,
therefore, ceases when people cease to fear terror - of
law or arms" is given by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
68. Who among the following was the editor of
Bombay Chronicle and was deported ?
questions.explanation:
Benjamin Guy Horniman
Benjamin Guy Horniman, a british journalist working
with Bombay Chronicle, defied the order and reported
fearlessly on the protests being held across India against
infamous Rowlatt Act. So he was deported.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:

influence on Mahatma Gandhi during his
formative period ?
questions.explanation:
John Stuart Mill
Gandhi was influenced by Raychandra Mehta John
Ruskin and Leo Tolstoy. Gandhi ji established
"Tolstoy" farm in South Africa on the name of Leo
Tolstoy.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText: 70. Who led the Mulshi Dam Satyagrah in 1922 ?
questions.explanation:
P.M. Bapat
The Mulshi dam Satyagraha was led by Pandurang
Mahadev (Senapati) Bapat, a socialist and nationalist
who had been educated in England, like Medha Patkar
of Narmada Andolan. Bapat was a leader of much
charisma and courage.

72. Which national leader stated in 1929 that
Congress was not a labour organisation but a
large body comprising all manner of people ?
questions.explanation:
Jawaharlal Nehru
Jawaharlal Nehru in 1929 stated that congress was not
a labour organisation but a large body comprising all
manner of people.
 Session of congress in 1929 was held in Lahore in
Chairmanship of J.L. Nehru. In this session Resolution
of "Purna Swarajya" was passed.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
73. Which Indian revolutionary abroad handed
over command of the I.N.A. to Subhas
Chandra Bose in 1943 ?
questions.explanation:
Rasbehari Bose
Rasbehari Bose transferred the control and leadership
of the Indian Independence league and the Indian
National Army to Subhash Chandra Bose. It must be
noted that it was the organisational spadework done by
Rasbehari Bose that Subhas could build up the Indian
National Army.
 Subhash Bose became supreme commander of INA
on August 25, 1944 (In Feb. 1944, after a collapse of
the lungs, Rasbehari's health deteriorated and he died on
January 1945 aged 58.)

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
74. When was States Reorganization Commission
appointed by Prime Minister Nehru ?
questions.explanation:
1953
Nehru government appointed the States Reorganisation
Commission (SRC) in August 1953. The commission
comprising justice Fazl Ali K.M. Pannikar and
Hridaynath
Kunzru
as
members.
Committee
submitted its report in October 1955.
In November 1956 "The States Reorganisation Act was
passed which provided for formation of fourteen states
and six Centrally administered territory.

questions.testName: UGC NET/JRF History July 2016 Paper III
questions.questionText:
75. Under
which
constitutional
reform,
the
Diarchy was introduced at provincial level ?
questions.explanation:
Montangue-Chelmsford Reforms (1919)
In line with the government policy contained in
Montangue's statement of August 1917, the government
announced further constitutional reforms in July 1918
known as Montangue Chelmsford Reform. Based on
these the "Government of India Act 1919" was enacted.
 The Act introduced dyarchy for the executive at the
level of provincial government. Dyarchy - rule of two -
executive councilors and popular ministers was
introduced.

the maintenance of a Buddhist monastery built
by Balaputradeva.

Kingdom of Srivijaya.

initially friendly, but later inimical.

monastery at Nagapatinam.

cordial relations with the kingdom of Srivijaya.
Rajendra I's relations with Srivijaya was initially
friendly, but later inimical. Mara Vijayottungavarman
built a Buddhist monastry at Nagapatnam.

The fourteenth century saint-poetess Lalla

Alauddin Khalji prohibited selling and
drinking of liquor in his territory. Alauddin analysed
causes of revolts and passes four ordinances. In his third
ordinance he prohibited liquor, gambelling etc.

Ibn Battuta given above description about

officers was called pradhan of the sarkar. In Mughal

unanimously prohibited so I left music.

All India Muslim League founded in 1906.

was as big an enemy as colonialism.

on USA and the USSR.
questions.explanation:
Non Align movement was started by Nehru,
President Tito and Abdul Nasser of Egypt. Five
criteria's of NAM–
(i) A country should follow an independent policy based
on peaceful co-existence and non alignment.
(ii) It should have consistently supported National
freedom movement in other countries.
(iii) It should not be a member of multi lateral alliances
concluded in context of super power conflicts.
(iv) If it has conceded military bases, these concessions
should not have been made in the context of super
power conflicts.
(v) If it is a member of bilateral or regional defence
arrangements, this should not be in the context of super
power politics.

(B) Cholas

(C) Palas

questions.explanation:

The Sailendra rulers of east indies maintained
intimate relations with Palas and Cholas. According to
Nalanda inscription king Devapaldeva of Bengal (Pala

War captives were major source of procuring
slaves.
questions.optionB: Slaves were sold in the open market.
questions.optionC:
If slave commits suicide, the owner should be
held responsible and be punished.
questions.optionD:
To execute the deed rakshapalas and residents
of the town were chosen as witness.
questions.explanation:
If slave commits suicide, the owner should be
held responsible and be punished.

Lekhapaddhati is sanskrit text at the time of
Chalukyas. It provides a glimpse of society under
Chalukyas. It shows slavery to be a common feature of
the society and people used to sell themselves to evade
famine and hunger. It further narrates story of a girl
who wanted to sell herself to evade harassment by
invader it also provides information about slave trade
between India and west Asian countries.

recommendation to the court for forfeiting the
zamindari rights.

A subadar of the province sometimes could
appoint a member of the same old family to
replace a recalcitrant zamindar.

A Mughal zamindar's income form its
proprietary claims (malikana) was 10 per cent
(25 per cent in Gujarat) to which was added
5–10 per cent nankar which he received from
revenue authorities in lieu of revenue

appoint a member of the same old family to replace a

landholders in villages. They had hereditary rights of
collecting land revenues which could go up to 25% of
the revenue. They generally made collection from
individual peasants at rates fixed by custom and paid
fixed tax to government.

(R):

Assertion (A) : The semi-divine origins of the
family of Chenghiz Khan coupled with the
enormous prestige of his success and career had
made his house an object of inspiration and owe
and had preserved sovereignty in his family upto
the 16th century.

Reason (R) : Such was the spell of the house of
Chenghiz Khan that even Timur thought it
advisable to exercise full power in the name of a
descendant of Chenghiz Khan and felt contended
with the humble title of Amir or Beg.

In the context of the above two statements,
which one of the following is correct?
questions.optionA:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.optionB:
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the
correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Chengiz Khan was the founder of great
Mangol empire which become the largest contiguous
empire in History after death. He came to power by
uniting many of the Namadic tribes of North-east.
Taimur believed himself descendant of Chengiz Khan
and felt contended with humble title of Amir or Beg.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2018 (18.12.2018) Paper II

37. "One camel goes for a penny (dang), but who
has a penny?"

In the above statement Ziauddin Barani is
referring to the state of affairs of which of the
following Sultan's reign?
questions.explanation:
The reign of Allauddin Khilji marks the
zenith of the Delhi Sultanate.
 He was the first muslim ruler to extend his empire
right up to the extreme South of India.
 During his time a system of price control had been set
up, reduced the salary amount that needed to be paid.
Three separate markets were set up in Delhi. The first
one for food grain, second for cloth, items such as ghee,
oil and sugar. The third market was horses, cattle and
slaves.
 He fixed the price of all the commodities from top to
bottom, market officers called Sahna were appointed to
keep a check on the prices. The defaulters were heavily
punished.

twenty years was leaning on a favourite, I
guessed that he must be the king. But the
people performed no courtesies or salutations

karori/amil (revenue collector) and amin

was fixed in Shahjahan's period?

questions.optionD: From 8 per cent it was reduced to 5 per cent
questions.explanation:
 The office of the Karori was created whose
task was to collect information and create assessments
of those Jagirs which could produce revenue of one
crore were to be put under an officer called

revenue Assessment.

was revised from 8 percent to 5%.

Comprehension for Question Nos. 113 to 116
Read the following account of Marco Polo and
answer the questions that follow:
These ships (plying in Arabian Sea) are wretched affairs,
and many of them get lost; for they have no iron
fastenings, and are only stitched together with twine
made from the husk of the Indian nut. They beat this
husk until it becomes like horse-hair and from that they
spin twine and with this stitch the planks of the ships
together. It keeps well, and is not corroded with the sea-
water, but it will not stand well in a storm. The ships are
not pitched, but are rubbed with fish-oil. They have mast,
sail and rudder, and have no deck, but only a cover
spread over the cargo when loaded. This cover consists
of hides, and on the top of these hides they put the
horses, which they take (from Hormuz) to India for sale.
They have no iron to make nails of and for this reason
they use only wooden tree-nails in their ship-building,
and then stitch the planks with twine as I have told you.
Hence it is a perilous business to go on a voyage in one
of those ships and many of them are lost, for in the Sea
of India the storms are often terrible.

"Once the Ahar Iron is disposed of, all 14 C
dates for the earliest iron levels in India appear
to cluster around 1000 BC or little earlier."
Whose opinion is this?
questions.explanation:
This view is of Irfan Habib. The coming of
Iron age is a long-debated one in the field of historical
studies while some Historians argue that the use of Iron
into India as a result of diffusion from the west some
argue that it developed independently Historians like
T.N. Roy. Argue for an early and late phase of Iron age
while Dilip K Chakrabarti and A. Ghosh do not
Argue for an early phase of Iron uses and place the
chronology at 1300 B.C. to 700 B.C. thus the period
from 1000 B.C. to 100 A.D. is archeologically reffered
to the study of Iron age. The Iron age sites in India are
associated with the finds of PGW pottery painted grey
ware has been found at most sites which have evidenced
use of Iron in the subcontinent.

Kavyadarsa is the earliest surviving systematic
treatise of poetics in Sanskrit composed by Dandin. It is
divided in 3 parichheds (parts).

Ashtadhyayi is ancient grammatical text written by
Panini in Sanskrit. It contains eight chapters each
divided in four parts.

Mahabhasya is attributed to Patanjali is a
commentary on selected rules of Sanskrit Grammar
from Panini's treatise as well as Katyayana's Varttika
an elaboration of Panini's grammar. It is dated to the
second century B.C.E.

Tantraloka "Light on tantra" is the master work
of Abhinavgupta who was the most revered Kashmir
Shaivism master on Tantra. A treasure text containing
the synthesis of 64 meniseus Agamas and all the
schools of tantra.

46. Regarding Taqavi loans, which of the following

surely for their repayment.

{(ii) and (iv) only}

Taqavi loan was a short term loan given to poor

surcharge on Taqavi loan.

loans so statement (iv) is wrong.

So answer is (d) (ii) and (iv) only.

questions.questionText:
53. A number of changes were introduced by
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq in Alauddin's agrarian
measures. Which of the following in this
context is NOT correct?
questions.optionA:
To lighten the burden of the peasants he
substituted hukm-i masahar (measurement) to
hukm-i hasil (crop sharing).
questions.optionB:
Ghiyasuddin did not believe in Alauddin's
principle of levelling down the village heads
to the rank of the ordinary peasant and
restored their perquisites.
questions.optionC:
He exempted their cultivation and pasturage
from assessment.
questions.optionD:
He also continued and encouraged the
practice of farming of the land revenue.
questions.explanation:
(He also continued and encouraged the
practice of farming of the land revenue.)

Solution : The reign of Allauddin Khaliji is known
for efforts of consolidating an empire militarily,
Administratively
and
economically
Ghiyasuddin
Tughluq founder of the Tughluq Dynasty. Who
assumed the throne was now faced with organizing a
new revenue system for his empire. In order to relieve
the peasantry of excessive taxation he brought the
system of 'Hukum-i-hasil' (method of measurement
based on crop sharing this allowed cultivators to
increase productivity Ghiyasuddin Tughluq's policy was
that gradually increasing the revenue collection in
proportion to increase in productivity.

The practice of revenue farming was discouraged
hence 4th option is correct.
