Who
propounded
the
theory
of
Sanskritization?
questions.explanation:
(M.N. Srinivas)

The concept of sanskritization was first introduced
by prof. M.N. Srinivas the famous sociologist. He
explained the concept of sanskritization in his book
"Religion and society among the coorgs of south
India."

Sanskritization is a process by which a lower caste
or tribe or any other group changes its customs, rituals,
Ideology and way of life in the direction of a higher.
Jahangir twice mentions a tower, tank and pavilion used
as a hunting palace about 29 km from Lahore. Today the
site is known as Shaikhupura, but Jahangir in 1606 refers
to it as Jahangirpura and then in 1620 calls it
Jahangirabad, both meaning City of Jahangir, the latter a
more Persianate from. Here the cmperor's favourite tame
antelope died before 1606; it was buried in a grave above
which a sculpted antelope and eulogy written by Mulla
Muhammad Husain of Kashmir were placed. Adjacent to
this gravestone, a tower was constructed around 1606
under the supervision of Sikandar Muin Khan, the
landholder of the area. On Jahangir's orders, Sikandar
Muin Khan also built a tank and royal residence. Despite
Muin's death while the work was in progress, the
complex was handsomely completed by 1620, the later
stages of construction having been supervised by Iradat
Khan. The expenses incurred were sufficiently awesome
that the emperor recorded the amount in his memoirs.
Jahangir considered the site a 'kingly hunting place',
although his successor found the place inadequate and in
1634 spent another sizable sum rebuilding the pavilion.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2019 (20.06.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
73. Under which system or settlement, the Indian
States lost their right to foreign affairs and
defense?
questions.explanation:
(Subsidiary alliance system)

Subsidiary alliance system was used by Lord
Wellesley under the system :
(1) Ruler was compelled to permanent stationing of
British force with, their territory and to pay subsidy
to maintenance.
(2) The rulers had to agree to the posting of British
resident in his court.
(3) No European can be employed in his service
without consultation with company.
(4) Nor he could go to war or negotiate with any other
Indian ruler without consulting governor general.

In return for all this British would defend the ruler
from his enemies and adopt a policy of non interference

administration incharge in mauryan administration as
astynomoi.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
14. Ferishta writes, "His country was well-peopled
and the subjects were submissive to his
authority. The rais of Malabar, Ceylon and
other countries kept ambassadors at his court
and set annually rich presents".

Identify this Vijayanagara ruler:
questions.explanation:
Vijayanagar empire was founded by two
brother Harihar and Bukka. Bukka I was called
Bukkaraj I. He belong to sangam dynasty. He reigned
21 years the kingdom prospered and continued to
expand in Southern India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
15. Which one of the following was not a revenue
free land grant?
questions.explanation:
Under Jahangir, some muslim nobles were
given Jagir resembling to watan Jagir called Al-tamgha.
Jagirs which involved no obligation of service and were
independent of rank were called Inam Jagirs.
Suyarghal term was used for grants of revenue in
charity in Akbar's administration.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
16. The long Palam Baoli inscription at Delhi in the
classical Sanskrit characteristically claims that
owing to the rulers 'benign rule', the God
Vishnu relinquishing all worries sleeps in peace
on the ocean of milk;. About which ruler it has
been claimed?
questions.explanation:
Ghiyasuddin Balban a slave of Iltutmish who
belong to Ilbari tribe of the Turks. He reigned Delhi
Sultanate from 1266 to 1287. The long palam Baoli
inscription
at
Delhi
in
the
classical
sanskrit
characteristically claims that owing to the rulers benign
rule the god Vishnu relinquishing all worries sleeps in
peace on the ocean of milk it is about Ghiyasuddin
Balban.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
17. Identify the Sultan who refused to implement
Shariat on the advice of a Quazi.
questions.explanation:
Alauddin called his theologian Qazi
Mughisuddin to his presence and told him what he had
been doing and each time asked him whether this was in
accordance with the shariat and each time the brave
Qazi said : No your majesty.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
18. Which of the following Sultans was earlier
known as Ali Gurshasp?
questions.explanation:
Alauddin known as Ali Gurshasp until his
Ascension in July, 1296. He was formally proclaimed as
the new king with the title Allauddunyad-din-
Muhammad Shah-is-Sultan at Kara. His reign period
was 1296 to 1316.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
19. In which travelogue the material condition of
the people of India has been described as
under:

"The common people lived in poverty so great
and miserable that the life of the people can be
depicted or accurately described only as the
home of stark want the dwelling place of bitter
woe".
questions.optionC:
Francois Bernier's Travels in the Mogul
Empire
questions.explanation:
Francisco Pelsaert the merchant with Dutch
East India company who stayed at Agra during 1620-27
wrote about "The utter subjection and poverty of the
common people. Poverty so great and miserable that the
life of people can be depicted or accurately described
only as the home of stark want and dwelling place of
bitter woe.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
20. In which language did Banarsidas write a very
interesting autobiography, the Ardh-Kathanak
in 1641?
questions.explanation:
Banarsi Das is known for his poetic
autobiography Ardhakathanaka (The Half Story)
composed in Braj Bhasa, an early dialect of Hindi
linked with the region around Mathura. It is the first
autobiography written in an Indian language.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
21. Concept of Watan-Jagir came into existence
towards the end of the reign of Emperor
questions.explanation:
The term Watan-Jagir came into existence
only at the end of reign of Akbar Jagirs in close
proximity to watan were considered a part of the Watan
and were not transferable except in case of rebellion etc.
These watan jagirs were granted for life within
Rajasthan.
Akbar followed the policy of Sulah-e-Kul.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
22. In the Mansabdari system do-aspa, Sih-aspa
was introduced by
questions.explanation:
The term do-aspa and Sih aspa was first used
in the 10th year of Jahangir's reign. It was however in
the reign of Shahjahan that it acquired a definite
meaning. This practice was continued by Aurangzeb, it
was a device to encourage the competent mansabdar.
 Jahangir's reign period was from 1605-1627.
 Jahangir handed a chain at the bank of Yamuna called
'chain of justice'.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
23. Who is known to have created autonomous
dominion comprising Bihar and Bengal in the
early 13th century?
questions.explanation:
Muhammad Bakhtyar Khalji was military
commander of the Delhi Sultanate founder Qutub-ud-
din Aibak who led the muslim conquests of Bengal and
Bihar and then become their ruler. His invasions are
believed to have severely damaged the Buddhist
establishments in East India.
Reign period of Kutub-ud-din Aibak was till 1206 to
1210. He is known as 'Lakh Bakhs' meaning 'giver of
lakhs'.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText: 24. Farman could be issued by
questions.explanation:
Farman is a mughal constitutional term
meaning an irrevocable royal decree issued by emperor.
A farman carries the form of a bill made law by the
assent of the head of the state. The emperor issued a
farman not just as he pleased. Some established
procedures were always observed while issuing an
Imperial Farman. in other words Farman is royal order
relating any matter in state.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
25. Which Mughal Emperor is known to have
celebrated Diwali in Srinagar, Kashmir?
questions.explanation:
Akbar started the tradition of celebrating
Diwali in his court. It become a part of the cultural
Ethics that mughals had developed in Hindustan. Apart
from the fireworks depicted in mughal paintings. We
hear of the Akash diya (The lamp in the sky) which was
lit on a high pale during Jasn-e-Chiragham (festival of
light).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
26. Which one of the following Mughal emperors
was impressed with the philosophy of Vedanta
and went to meet Jadrup Gosain?
questions.explanation:
Jahangir got impressed with a Jain saint and
took Diksha and named himself as Jagat and Jodha bai
as Jagat Gosain like his father Akbar he converted many
hindu texts in persian and asserted there was not much
difference between sufism in Islam and Vedant
philosophy in Hindus. Jahangir met Jadrup Gosain a
Jain saint in Ujjain.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
27. 'The military forces were reorganized by the
Sultan.
The
Commander-in-Chief
was
henceforth called Amirul Umara and a group
of officers, called barbardaran, was created
whose duty it was to mobilize troops in time of
need. There were, besides, two hundred Yakka
Jawans or Silahdaran whose duty it was to

Sultan had 4,000 bodyguards who were called
Khasahkhel'.

Identify this Bahmani sultan of Gulbarga:
questions.explanation:
Muhammad I reigned 1358 to 1375 his
predecessor was Allauddin Bahaman Shah and his
successor was Mujahid Shah. Muhammad Shah I
inflicted such a devastating blow on zamindars of
carnatic that he massacred 5 lakh people from the land
and looted wealth accumulated of 500 years it is said by
Farishta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
28. 'Star of India', a non-hereditary order of
knighthood for both Europeans and Indians,
began to be awarded from which year?
questions.explanation:
The star of India was an order of knighthood
for services to the empire, set up by the first viceroy
Lord Canning and Sir Charleswood of the India office.
It was awarded to high ranking Indians as well as
Europeans. The first such orders were presented on 1st
November, 1861 at Allahabad.
Lord Canning was last governor general of India. revolt
of 1857 arose at the time period of Canning.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
29. Who among the following stated: "I wish to
have a different and rival spirit in different
regiments, so that Sikh might fire into Hindoo,
Gorkha into either, without any scruple in case
of need"?
questions.explanation:
(Charles Wood)

Charles wood the secretary of state for India said "I
wish to have a different and rival spirit in different
regiments so that Sikh might fire into Hindu. Gorakha
into either without any scruple in case of need".

Sir Charles Wood's notable work is 'wood's
dispatch' according to wood's dispatch vernacular
education started in India and three universities.
Bombay, Madras & Kolkata established as per the
recommendation of wood's dispatch.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
30. Which play written by Dinbandhu Mitra
exposes the exploitation of plantation workers
in Bengal?
questions.explanation:
(Neel Darpan)

In 1860. Dinbandhu Mitra a Bengali civil servant
wrote Neel Darpan (The Indigo mirror), a political play
that exposed the exploitative conditions of Indigo
Plantations of Bengal and the British planters.

Lilavati is Indian mathematician Bhaskara II's

Kamale Kamini is composed by Dinbandhu Mitra.

Lilavati is also composed by Dinbandhu Mitra.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
31. Which among the following tribes of Palamau
(Ranchi) kept aloof from the 1857 uprising?
questions.explanation:
Mundas and Oraons

Nilamber and Pitamber were freedom fighters from
Jharkhand, two brothers had led a revolt against the East
India Company in 1857 they were born in Chemo-snya
village in the Bhogta clan of the Kharwar in Latehar
district. Mundas and Oraons kept aloof from 1857
uprising.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:

one
of
the
following
statements

questions.optionA:
The decline of courtly patronage in the

questions.optionB:

questions.optionC:
The emergence of nation as a community

The newly developed interest in music, its

by nationalist ideals.
questions.explanation:
The newly developed interest in music, its
practice and performance was solely inspired by
nationalist ideals.

There was significant impact of nationalist Ideas on
modern Indian music but not complete.

of Musical nationalism is the term used to describe
art music that was created with the Intension to promote
nationalism. The 19th century also known as the
Romantic Era was a turbulent political time in the
western world.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:

social change in the nineteenth century?

"All progress in social liberation tends to be a
change from the law of status to the law of
contract, from the restraints of family and
caste, customs to the self-imposed restraints of
the free will of the individual".
questions.explanation:

Keshub Chandra Sen founder of Brahmo Samaj of

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
34. In which year did the Bengal Police for the first
time, use the method of finger printing for
crime detection and proof?
questions.explanation:
(1898)

Fingerprints are very useful for the purpose of
identification
of
criminals
and
proving
their
participation in court. The earliest known fingerprints
being used as signatures for Identification are from
Baby lone. Towards the end of 19th century sir Edward
Richard Henry IG of police lower provinces Bengal.
Started maintaining criminal records through a
mathematical formula of fingerprint patterns in 1898.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

questions.explanation:
(Mahad sweet water tank satyagrah)
All other movements given in option are led by Gandhi
ji. Kheda Satyagraha started in 1918. Gandhi ji was
spiritual head of Satyagraha. In 1918 the crops failed in
Kheda district of Gujrat but revenue not remitted

Vallabh Bhai Patel lead the Satyagraha at ground level.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
questions.explanation:

Purshotamdas Thakurdas was a moderate leader and
always favoured the co-ordination with British

Gandhi Irwin pact at the Karachi session (1931) of
Congress.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:

"No Indian could have started the Indian
National Congress... If an Indian had come
forward to start such a movement embracing
all India, the officials, in India would not have
allowed the movement to come into existence. If
the founder of the congress had not been a
great Englishman, such was the distrust of
political agitation in those days that the
authorities would have at once found some way
or the other to suppress the movement".

Select correct option:
questions.explanation:
(Gopal Krishna Gokhale)

Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a social reformer and
political leader of Indian National Congress during the
time of the Indian Independent movement. He was the
founder of "The servants of India Society". He was
the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi. In year 1915 he
died.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:

is contemporary history"?
questions.explanation:
(Beneditto Croce)

Beneditto
Croce
was
an
Italian,
Idealist,
Philosopher historian & Politician who wrote on
numerous topics. He said, "All history is contemporary

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
39. From
among
the
following
statements
regarding the precautions a historian must
observe, which one is not correct?
questions.optionA:
He should not introduce in the text that is not
said by the author.
questions.optionB:
Facts obtained by direct examination of the
document must not be confused with the
results obtained by reasoning.
questions.optionC:
If the reasoning leaves any doubt, conclusion
should be drawn by constructive imagination
questions.optionD:
The historian should not invent what is not
already existing.
questions.explanation:
If the reasoning leaves any doubt, conclusion
should be drawn by constructive imagination. It is not
correct,
because
history
comprise
sources
of
Information, Analysis, Synthesis of facts there is no
scope of imaginary conclusion in history.

external criticism (Heuristic operations) in
historical writing, is not correct?
questions.optionA: To establish the authorship of the document
questions.optionC: To determine the place of the document
questions.optionD:
To fix the time of the document, the exact
date, month and year of writing
questions.explanation:
To carry out interpretative criticism historical
evidence is derived from historical data by the process
of criticism which is of two types : External and
Internal.
External
criticism
is
concerned
with
establishing the authenticity of data. It is also called
lower criticism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

2. Harshavardhana

3. Rudradaman

4. Samudragupta

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(1 and 4)

Samudragupta was a musician. He was a good
player of Vina. Kharvela entertained the people of
Kalinganagari in the third year of his reign. The king
himself was well versed in 'Gandharva veda' (arts and
sciences of music).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:
42. Which of the following are true about the
stupa?

(1) The Buddha had enjoined the erection of
stupas over his ashes

(2) The custom of rearing stupas was pre-
Buddhist

(3) The Jainas also erected this form of memorial
in early times

(4) The extent Dhamekha stupa of Sarnath is one
of the oldest

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
(1, 2 and 3 only)

Buddha never ordered about the construction of
stupa on his remains. A Brahmin Drona divided the
relics into eight parts. After the Buddha's Parinirbbana
his relics were enshrined and worshipped in stupas by
the royals of eight countries.

Jaina never created stupa kind of memorial in the
early period.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

4. Vitasta

questions.explanation:
(1, 2 and 3 only)

Harirud, Kubha and Krummu rivers were located in
Afghanistan.

Vitasta now Jhelam river flows in Panjab region

Sindhu (Indus) river have seven tributaries so Indus
region is called "Saptasaindhav Pradesh".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

Megasthenes's original record about India is lost
some of his memories are preserved in accounts of
Arrian, Diodoras, pliny and strabo.

"Herodotus is called "father of history".

Diodoras
was
Greek
historian
known
for
'Bibliatheca Historica'.

Arrian wrote two books "Indica & Anabasis of
Alexander".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

2. Bhasa

3. Bharavi
4. Kalidasa

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II

2. Bhoja Paramara

questions.explanation:

Harshavardhana,
Bhoj

and

Erragudi, near Gooty, Kurnool district, Andhra

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2019 (02.12.2019) Paper II
questions.questionText:

Questions Numbers (96-100):
Read the following passage and answer the questions
that follow.
The revolt of 1857 was much more than a mere
product of sepoy discontent. It was in reality a
product of accumulated grievances against the
company's administration, a popular discontent and
hatred against foreign rule. The most important
cause was the economic exploitation, the complete
destruction of its traditional economic fabric, the
impoverishment of the vast mass of peasants, artisans
and handicraftsmen as also a large number of
traditional zamindars and chiefs. As a result of the
British land and revenue policies and the system of
Judicial administration, a large number of peasant
proprietors lost their land to traders and money-
lenders and found themselves in utter debt. In
addition, the common people were hard hit by
corruption even at the lower levels of administration.
The complex judicial system enabled the rich to
oppress the poor, and the growing poverty made
them desperate. The middle and upper classes of
Indian society suffered by their exclusion from higher
positions in the administration. Displacement of
Indian rulers led to the loss of patronage to the men
of arts and culture and also to the religious
preachers–pandits and Maulvis, who played an
important role in spreading discontent against the
government. Besides, Lord Dalhousie's policy of
annexations of native states by applying the 'Doctrine
of Lapse' was widely resented. Lastly, the conversion
activities by the Christian missionaries created fear
and suspicion among the general public.

are obedient to me in proper way"

Identify the person whom Sultan Alauddin
Khalji was complaining to?
questions.explanation:
Allauddin
Khalji
complains
Qazi
Mughisuddin "Not even a hundred karohs of my
territory are obedient in proper way".
Allauddin Khalji stated "I do what I think is in the best
interest of the state. I do not care whether it confirms to
the shariat or not.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
8.
Which of the following was not discovered by
Aryabhatta?
questions.optionB: The earth rotates on its axis
questions.optionC: The earth revolves around the sun
questions.optionD:
The shadow of the earth falling on the moon
causes eclipses
questions.explanation:
Aryabhatta was a Indian mathematician and
astronomer. Aryabhatta find out value of 'pi'.
Aryabhatta discovered the earth is sphere. The earth
rotates on its axis and the shadow of the earth falling on
the moon causes eclipses.
Aryabhatta given geocentric theory.
[Exam Date: 09.10.2020] Shift-I

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
9.
The first epigraphic evidence of Sati is found in
which of the following inscriptions?
questions.explanation:
Eran Pillar inscription is found from Eran ,
Sagar district Madhya Pradesh. It describes the battle
between Bhanugupta and Hun invador Tormana.
Goparaj a feudatary of Bhanugupta was killed during
the battle and his wife entered into the mass of fire. It is
first Archaeological evidence of sati pratha.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 10. What is the meaning of the Burunjis?
questions.optionA: The name of a hill Tribe in Nepal
questions.optionB:
The name of a recently discovered Neolithic
site in Kashmir
questions.explanation:
Burunjis are a class of historical genealogical
and manuscripts associated with the Ahom Kingdom.
There were two types of Burunjis first official compiled
from the time of Ahom king Sukaphaa and family and
Second Burunjis which were compiled from the 16th
century.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
11. Who among the following Gupta ruler issued
gold coins with the lowest percentage of gold?
questions.explanation:
The percentage of gold in Indian coins under
the reign of Gupta rulers showed a steady financial
decline over centuries as it decreases from 90% pure
gold under Chandragupta to a mere 75-80%. Under
Vishnugupta so right answer is Vishnugupta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
12. The involvement of ladies in the administration
was a feature of which of the following
dynasties?
questions.explanation:
Chalukya dynasties were frequently assigned
to the ladies high ranking position in administration. In
this period society become increasingly sophisticated.
The status of women was varied.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
13. A manuscript of Dhammapada written in
Kharoshthi script was found from which of the
following places?
questions.explanation:
In 1892 a copy of Dhammapada written in
Gandhari prakrat was discovered near Khotan in
Xinjiang. It was broken up and came to Europe in part
some going to Russia and some France but
unfortunately a portion of manuscript never appeared on
the market and seems to have been lost.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
14. Identify the Sultan who started the practice of
putting on the tanka the name of the mint
town:
questions.explanation:
Iltutmish established the Silver Tanka and the
bullion. Iltutmish may also be credited with extending
to India the trans frontier practice of putting on the
Tanka the name of the mint town.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
15. The Sultan himself used to take keen personal
interest in the development of agriculture. He
abolished zakat (import duty) on grain and
introduced a measurement standard, which
continued to prevail till the Mughal period.
Who was this Sultan?
questions.explanation:
Sikankar Lodi was an Afghan Sultan of Delhi
Sultanate between 1489 and 1517. He took personal
interest in agriculture and introduced a measurement
standard "Gaz-i-Sikandari" which continue to prevail
till the Mughal period.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
16. Amrit Kund, which deals with different
exercises
and
practices
for
health,
was
translated into Persian under which of the
following titles?
questions.explanation:
Hauz-ul Hayat a persian book published by
Muhammad Ghanith which is the translation of book
named amritkunda which mentions different exercises
and practices for health.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
17. The Mughal emperors wanted to control the
nomadic pastoral tribes of Sind because:
questions.optionA: they wanted to proselytize them to Islam
questions.optionB:
they wanted to bring them under the influence
of Suhrawardi sufi silsilah
questions.optionC:
they wanted to make them sedentary to
enhance the imperial income
questions.optionD:
they wanted to acquire their huge live stock
for their use
questions.explanation:
They wanted to make them sedentary to
enhance the imperial income.
Namadic pastoral tribes earn their livelihood from
grazing and gathering forest based materials they travel
from one region to other region for grazing so there is
difficult to regulate them. Hence Mughal wanted to
stabilize the pastoral tribes for revenue purpose.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
18. Which of the following Malwa Sultans had
constructed a grand Darul Shifa (hospital) in
Mandu?
questions.explanation:
Mahmud Khalji I a ruler of Malwa Sultanate
completed Jama masjid and Tomb of Hoshangabad. He
also builds a victory tower that constructed to
commemorate his victory over Rana Kumbha of
Mewar. Mahmud Khalji also constructed a hospital
(Darul Shifa) in Mandu in 1445. He gave land grants for
its maintenance with his own physician being appointed
to supervise the hospital.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
19. Which of the following Raja/Sultan/poet was
entitled Gandharva on account of his genius in
the field of music?
questions.explanation:
Sultan Hussain Shah was last ruler of Jaunpur
Sultanate in the Sharqi dynasty. He assumed the title of
Gandharva and contributed significantly in
the
development of Khayal a genre of Hindustani classical
music.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
20. Who drew the attention of Babur to the fact
that during Sikandar Lodi's regime the Hindus
look to learning Persian and were recruited in
large numbers to different posts?
questions.explanation:
Shaikh Abdul Quddus Gangohi a Indian Sufi
scholar from sufi silsilah drew the attention of Babur to
the fact that during Sikandar Lodi's regime the Hindus
took to learning persian and were recruited in large
numbers to different posts.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
21. Which of the following is not a prem-margi
nirguna bhakti saint?
questions.explanation:
Maluk Das was an devotional poet. He
believed in oneness of God. The Emperor Aurangzeb
recognised Das's value and denoted two villages to him
and his disciples.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
22. Which one of the following contains the
biographies of the sufis of India and the author
presented it to Jahangir?
questions.explanation:
Akhbar-ul Akhyar composed by Abdul Haq
Mahaddi Dehalvi, is a compilation of short biographies
of Sufi saints in India.
Masir-ul Umara - Samsam Ud daula Shah Nawaz Khan.
Tazkirat-ul Umara - S.M. Azizuddin Hussain.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
23. The illustrated copy of Shahnama of the late
sixteenth century Mughal school was prepared
at the library of which of the following
Prince/noble?
questions.explanation:
The illustrated copy of Shahnama of the late
16th century Mughal school was prepared at the library
of Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana. Abdul Rahim Khan-i-
Khana was among the Navratna's of Akbar. He had
been written dohas in Hindi and persian. He translated
Baburnama
from
Chagatai language to persian
language. In Sanskrit he wrote a book on astrology
"Khetakautukam"
and
Dwatrimshadyogavali
in
Devanagri script.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
24. The earliest mention of the use of belt drive for
powering gem-cutting comes from which of the
following travelers accounts?
questions.explanation:
Tavernier and Fryer mentioned the use of belt
drives for powering gem cutting.
Fryer was english doctor and traveler. He published his
account "New account of East India and Persia in
eight letters" in 1698.
Tavernier was a French explorer and merchant. He was
the first European to describe the diamond mines in
India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
25. Which of the following is the earliest known
account of the medieval bhaktas to be found in
a single work?
questions.explanation:
Bhaktamal is a poem in the Braja language
that gives short biographies of more than two hundred
Bhaktas, it was written by Guru Nabha Das ji.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
26. With regard to Tamil Siddhas which of the
following is not correct?
questions.optionA:
Tirumular was the greatest of the Tamil
Siddhas
questions.optionB:
Tamil Siddhism shows features of anti-
Brahmanism and anti-ritualism
questions.optionC:
Tamil
Siddhas
laid
emphasis
on
the
importance of Siva and Murugan the Tamil
deity
questions.optionD:
The chief centers of Tamil Siddhas were
Tondinadu and Pandinadu
questions.explanation:
Siddhas also called Siddhar were Tamil
saints, they were anti brahminism and anti ritualism.
Tirumular was greatest saint of this sect. They
emphasized worship of Siva and Murugan (Kartikeya)
Tamil deity.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
27. By 1914, about three quarters of the Indian
infantry came from which of the following
regions?
questions.optionC:
Punjab, Nepal and North-West Frontier
Province
questions.explanation:
After the Revolt of 1857 army was
reorganised because army was in forefront of the 1857
outbreak. Britishers followed policy of division and
counterpoise. They recruited most of armymen from
martial races of Punjab. Nepal and NWFP. Bengal,
Bihar and Awadh took active role in revolt so
recruitment of army from these states declined.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
28. When was the infamous Section 124-A relating
to 'sedition' was incorporated into the Indian
Penal
questions.explanation:
Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code lays
down punishment for sedition. It included in Indian
Penal Code in 1870 with Section 121A.
Indian Penal Code (IPC) was enacted in 1860 under the
British raj.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
29. In 1850, on the eve of the rise of large scale
industry in India, which of the following was
the most prominent community engaged in the
trade of the two principle exportable goods
from the western coast, cotton and opium?
questions.explanation:
Chettiar is a title used by many mercantile,
weaving agricultural and land owning castes in South
India especially in the states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
This was most prominent trading community in 1850.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
30. Who among the following was not associated
with the Lahore resolution adopted by the
Muslim League on 23 March, 1940?
questions.explanation:
Lahore resolution for the establishment of a
separate homeland for the muslims of British India
passed in the annual session of All India muslim league
held in Lahore on 22-24 March, 1940. Fazlul Haq,
Khaliquzzaman and Sikandar Hayat Khan were the
main leaders of Lahore resolution.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
31. Which one of the reformist Muslim leaders
published a modernist urdu journal Tahzib ul-
akhlaq?
questions.explanation:
Tahzib-ul-Akhlak a journal published by
muslim reformer Sir Syed Ahmad Khan between 1871
and 1897. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan emphasized on
Muslim education.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
32. Who established on January 15, 1876, the
Indian Association for the Cultivation of
Science in Calcutta?
questions.explanation:
Indian association for cultivation of science
in Calcutta founded in year 1876 by Dr. Mahendra Lal
Sarkar, an acclaimed medical practitioner of his time.
IACS is the oldest scientific institution in Asia funded
by department of science and technology government of
India and the government of West Bengal.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
33. Who summed up the motive behind the
partition of Bengal as. "Bengal united is a
power. Bengal divided will pull in several
ways"?
questions.explanation:
H.H. Risley gives statement "Bengal united
is a power. Bengal divided will pull in several ways".
The Bengal was divided by Lord Curzon in 1905
because Bengal was nerve center for nationalist activity.
British government tell the reason for partition of
Bengal inconvenience in administration.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
34. Who among the following was leading the
defence in the trials against the members of
INA?
questions.explanation:
Bhulabhai Desai was an Indian Independent
activist and acclaimed lawyer. He is well remembered
for his defence of the three Indian National Army
soldiers accused of treason during World War II.
Indian National Army was founded by Ras Bihari Bose.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
35. Which one of the following was not an ideal of
Arya Samaj?
questions.optionA: Belief in the authority of the Shastri class
questions.optionB: Fatherhood of God and brotherhood of man
questions.explanation:
Arya Samaj was established by Swami
Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay. Ideals of
Arya Samaj are–
(1) Fatherhood of God and Brotherhood of man.
(2) Equality of the gender.
(3) Suddhi movement
(4) Absolute justice and fair play between man and man
and nation and nation.
(5) Intercaste marriages and widow remarriages were
also encouraged.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
36. In which year was the All India Women's
Conference was formed?
questions.explanation:
The All India Women's Conference (AIWC)
is a non-government organisation. It was founded in
1927 by Margaret Cousins in Pune in order to improve
educational efforts for woman and children and has
expanded its scope to also tackle other women's right
issues.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
37. When did the French finally handed over their
Indian territories to India?
questions.explanation:
The french finally handed over their
territories to India in 1954.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
38. The Maharaja of which of the following states
signed the instrument of accession only after a
last minute theatrical show of defiance?
questions.explanation:
The Maharaja of Jodhpur Hanvant Singh
signed the instrument of accession only after a last
minute theatrical show of Defiance.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
39. In 1936, which of the following created as
'Anti-imperialist People Front' within the
Congress?
questions.explanation:
R.P. Dutt and Ben Bradley a marxist leader
created an "Anti Imperialist Front" in 1936 within
congress.
Congress socialist party was formed in late 1934.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
40. According to the Calcutta and Howrah Smoke
Nuisance Act the emissions of jute mills were
made subject to regulation. In which year this
act was passed by the Bengal Council?
questions.explanation:
Calcutta and Howrah Smoke Nuisance Act
was passed in 1863 by Bengal council. This act passed
because steam engines that ran on coal came up and
several jute mills and other industries were built on the
river Hooghly. So there was need to regulate
emmissions of jute mills.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
41. Which of the following are found in the
Neolithic cultures of India?

1. Ground and polished stone tools

2. Ploughs

3. Bullock carts

4. Domesticated barley and field pea

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Ground and polished stone tools and
domesticated barley and field pea are found from
neolithic cultures of India. There is no Archaeological
evidence of plough and bullock carts in neolithic period.
Neolithic period is from 700 BC to 1000 BC.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
42. Which of the following are associated with the
Megalithic cultures of India?

1. Iron tools and implements

2. Horses

3. Jorwe ware

4. Sarcophagi

5. Dolmens

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Iron tools and implements, Horses,
Sarcophagi and Dolmens are associated with megalithic
cultures of India. Jorwe were not found from megalithic
cultures of India.
A Megalith is a large prehistoric stone that has been
used to construct a monument or structure either alone
or together with other stones. Most extent megaliths
were erected between the neolithic period through the
chalcolithic period and into Bronze age.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
43. Which of the following sites have yielded the
'separate rock edicts' of Asoka?

1. Dhauli

2. Jaugada

3. Sannati

4. Udegolam

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
There are 14 "separate rock edicts" of
Ashoka. Dhauli, Jaugada and sannati are from them.
Ashoka left "Bherighosh" after the Kalinga war and
adopted Buddhism he adopted "Dhammaghosh". He
inscribed so much inscriptions subject of inscription is
Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
44. Which of the following are the salient features
of Mahayana Buddhism?

1. Worship of the Buddha image

2. Assimilation of local cults

3. The concept of the bodhisattva

4. Use of Pali for propagating Buddhism

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
After the 4th Buddhist council 98(AD)
Buddhism divided into two sects Hinayana and
Mahayana.
Salient features of Mahayana–
(1) Worship of Buddha image
(2) Assimilation of local cults
(3) The concept of bodhisattva
(4) They favoured sanskrit languge not pali.
(5) It is known as northern Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
45. Gupta emperor Chandragupta II was known
by which other following names?

1. Devagupta

2. Devaraja

3. Devaputra

4. Devavrata

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Chandragupta II "Vikramaditya" was known
as names Devagupta and Devaraja. Chandragupta II
succeeded Ramgupta by killing him. He extended limit
of empire by matrimonial alliances (with Nagas and
vakataks) and conquests (Western India). Chandragupta
II succeeded by Kumargupta I.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
46. Which of the following are the famous
commentators on the Manu Smriti?

1. Apararka

2. Kulluka

3. Medhatithi

4. Vijnanesvara

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Kulluka and Medhatithi are famous
commentators of Manu Smriti.
Manu Smriti is an ancient legal text and constitution
among the many Dharmashastras of Hinduism. It was
one of the first Sanskrit texts to have been translated
into english in 1776 by british philogist Sir William
Jones and was used to construct Hindu law.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
47. Which of the following statements about
Alberuni and his account of India are correct?

1. He was exiled and ordered to spend ten
years in India

2. According to him, people of untouchable
castes could live only outside the villages and
towns of the four castes

3. He supported the views of Brahamagupta
about the true nature of eclipses

4. According to him, the Hindus think that
there is no country like theirs and no
religion like theirs

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Alberuni a iranian scholar wrote "Tahkik-i-
hind" in which he mentioned that he was exiled and
ordered to spend ten years in India. He wrote about
Indian society that people of untouchable castes could
live outside the villages and towns. According to him,
the Hindus think that there is no country like theirs and
no religion like theirs. So the correct answer is (b).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
48. Which of the following temples are brick
temples?

1. Bhitargaon temple, Kanpur

2. Parsurameswara temple, Bhubaneshwar

3. Laxmana temple, Khajuraho

4. Laxmana temple, Sirpur
questions.explanation:
Bhitargaon temple, Kanpur is ancient Hindu
temple. It is the largest Indian brick temples to survive
from the time of Gupta Empire. It is dated 5th century.
Laxmana temple, Sirpur was built by the mother of
Mahasivagupta Balarjuna during 7th century AD
dedicated to Lord Vishnu, it is regarded as one of the
best examples of brick temples in India. The temple was
discovered by the Lord Cunningham in the year 1872.
The temple gets its name from a small black statue of
Lakshmana seated below a snakehood.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
49. Which of the following weapons arrived with
the Arabs when they invaded Sind in 712?

1. Naphtha

2. Hawai

3. Ban

4. Manjaniq

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Naphtha and Manjaniq are fearful weapons
arrived with the Arabs when they invaded sindh in 712.
Mohammad Bin Kasim attacked on sindh in 712 A.D. at
that time the king of Sindh was King Dahir. This battle
is called Battle of Rewa. Muhammad Bin Kashim
defeated Dahir. This battle is considered first muslim
invasion on India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
50. With regard to education, which of the
following statements are correct?

1. Iltutmish founded the Nasiriyya madrasa at
Delhi in memory of his son prince Nasir-ud-
din Mahmud

2. Razia appointed Minhaj Siraj as its
principal

3. The Firuz Shahi madrasa was founded by
Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq on the banks of
Yamuna at Ghiyaspur

4. The aristocracy engaged male and female
tutors for their sons and daughters

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
(1) Iltutmish founded the Nasiriyya madrasa
at Delhi in memory of his son prince Nasir-ud-din
Mahmud is correct.
(2) Razia appointed Minhaj Siraj as its principal is
correct.
(3) The Firuz Shahi madrasa was founded by Sultan
Firuz Shah Tughlaq on the banks of Yamuna at
Ghiyaspur is not correct because village surrounding
Firuzshahi Madarasa is called Tarabad (city of joy).
(4) The aristocracy engaged male and female tutors for
their sons and daughters is correct.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
51. In regard of token currency issued by Sultan
Muhmmad Tughlaq, which of the following
statements are correct?

1. According to Barani, the metal used for the
token coins was copper

2. While other coins had only Arabic super
inscriptions, the token coin had its legends
in Persian also

3. No care was taken to make the legend on the
token coins clear and legible

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Token currency was issued by Muhammad
Tughlaq for combatting crisis of precious metals.
(a) According to Barani, the metal used for the token
coins was copper is correct.
(b) Ferishta says it was brass or bronze is correct.
(c) While other coins had only arabic super inscriptions
the token coin had it legends in persian also is correct.
(d) No care was taken to make legend on the token
coins clear and legible is not make beyond the token
coins clear and legible.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History June 2020 (09.10.2020, S-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
52. With regard to the Afghan policy, which of the
following statements are correct?
1. Unlike Bahlol, Sikandar Lodi started
sitting on a throne, no noble could share the
seat with him
2. He still believed in primus inter pares (a
first among equals)
3. In order to impress the superior position of
the Sultan on the minds of the nobles and
the people, he laid down elaborate rules for
the reception of royal farmans in the
distant parts of the kingdoms

in the agrarian and revenue structure of the

the following provisions are correct?

revenue collection

- pahani)

3. Under nazar-pahani land was divided into
baghat and nabud

4. The maximum rate of land revenue was
decided between 1/4 and 2/5 of the produce on
different classes of soil

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
(1) Malik amber abolished the farming of
land revenue collection is correct.
(2) He initiated "Nazar pahani system of glance survey"
is correct.
(3) Under "Nazar Pahani" land was divided into Baghat
and Nabud is not correct.

between 1/4 to 2/3 of produce on different classes of
soils is correct.
Malik amber was Prime Minister of Ahmadnagar
Sultanate. He founded Aurangabad. He built Janjira fort
also.

salaries of the Begums and Princes

given below:

period.

ministers, grandees of the Mughal empire is correct.

of the emperor is correct.

parvanchas were not issued for the stipulated salaries of

Read the following passage from the Arthashastra of
Kautilya, and answer the following questions:

The Superintendent of cattle should know about
cattle looked after in return for a wage, tended with a tax
and a fixed return, become useless and cast off, entered
in the state hards by payment of a shares the total number
of cattle in herds, cattle that are lost or have perished,
and the total produce of milk and ghee. The cowherd, the
buffalo-herdsman, the milker, the churner and the hunter
should look after do one hundred milch-cows, receiving
a wage in cash. For, if given a wage in milk and ghee,
they might do harm to the calves. These are cattle looked
after for a wage. One person should look after one
hundred animals containing an equal number of aged
cows, milch-cows, cows with young, cows with calf for
this first and heifers. He should give eight vasrakas of
ghee, one pana per animal and the hide with the mark,
every year. This is tending with a tax and a fixed return.
Herdsmen looking after one hundred animals divided
into an equal number of cows that are diseased, that are
crippled, that do not allow another person to milk them,
that are difficult to milk and that kill their calves, should
give a share appropriate to that class. These are cattle
become useless and cast off.

Read the following passage and answer the questions

The Timariots, Governors and Revenue contractors
on their part, reason in this manner. Why should the
neglected state of this land create uneasiness in our
minds? And why should we expend our money and time
to render it fruitful? We may be deprived of it in a single
moment and our exertions would benefit neither
ourselves nor our children. Let us draw from the soil all
the money we can, though the peasant should starve or
abscond and we should leave it, when commanded to
quit, a dreary wilderness.

Statement (A), (B) and (C) are correct about
Mughal paintings during Jahangir's period that–
 Mansur was expert in painting animals and flowers.
 Abdul Hasan was a portraitist.
 Govardhan was an expert painter of painting holymen,
musicians, and eccentrics.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
4.
Digambar Biswas and Bishnu Biswas led which
of the following movement in 1859-60?
questions.explanation:
The Indigo revolt started in the villages of
Gobindapur and Chaugacha where Bishnu Vishwas and
Digambar Biswas first led the rebellion against planters
in Bengal (1859). The Indigo depots were burned down.
Many planters fled to avoid being caught.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
5.
Which of the following inscriptions suggests a
time reckoning starting from the Bharata war?
questions.explanation:
Aihole inscription of Pulakesin-II suggests a
time reckoning starting from the Bharata war. Aihole
inscription is in sanskrit language and old kannada
script. It mentions 3103 B.C. as date of Mahabharata
war.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
6.
Which of the following officers were known for
water arrangement of their provinces?

(A) Suyya

(B) Pushyagupta

(C) Tushaspa

(D) Suvisakha

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Suyya, Pushyagupta, Tushaspa and
Suvisakha were the officers known for water
arrangement in their provinces.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
7.
From
among
the
following
statements
regarding economic critique of colonialism,
which ones are correct?

(A)
The British administrators attributed the
rapid construction of railroads and the growth
of India's foreign trade as a proof of India's
prosperity

(B)
For nationalists, a negative impact on
indigenous
industries,
foreign
trade
and
railways
represented
India's
underdevelopment of economy

(C)
The nationalists emphasized that while
expenditure served British imperial needs, it
also brought consequent prosperity to Indian
people

(D)
Not until 1905, did the drain theory form
part of the Indian National Congress agenda

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) and (B) are correct regarding
critique of colonialism that
 British administrators attributed the rapid construction
of railroads and the growth of India's foreign trade as a
proof of India's prosperity.
 For nationalists, a negative impact on indigenous
industries, foreign trade and railways represented India's
underdevelopment of economy.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
8. Which of the following historians claimed that
Akbar's empire in 1592 was said to contain as
many as 120 cities and 3,200 towns?
questions.explanation:
Nizamuddin Ahmad claimed that Akbar's
empire in 1592 was said to contain as many as 120
cities and 3,200 towns.
 Nizamuddin Ahmad composed a book Tabqat-i-
Akbari which is a comprehensive work on general
history covering the time from Ghaznavids up to the
38th year of Akbar's reign.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
9.
Chronologically arrange the following treaties
starting from the earliest:

(A)
The Treaty of Srirangpattanam

(B)
The Treaty of Lahore

(C)
The Treaty of Bassien (Vasai)

(D)
The Treaty of Allahabad and Kara

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Chronological order of treaties–
(D) The Treaty of Allahabad and Kara - 1765
(A) The Treaty of Srirangpattanam - 1792
(C) The Treaty of Bassien (Vasai) - 1802
(B) The Treaty of Lahore - 1846

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
10. Given below are two statements:

Statement (I): Hoes and sickles, small weapons
and horse trappings of iron have been found at
megalithic sites.

Statement (II): Maski and Nagarjunakonda are
megalithic sites.

In the light of the above statements, choose the
most appropriate answer from the options given
below:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement (I) is true but statement (II) is false
questions.optionD: Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true
questions.explanation:
Statement (I) is correct Hoes and sickles,
small weapons and horse trappings of iron have been
found at megalithic sites.
Statement (II) is correct that Maski and Nagarjunakonda
are megalithic sites.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
11. Which of the following texts allow divorce?

(A) Narada Smriti

(B) Manava Dharmasastra

(C) Arthasastra

(D) Yajnavalkya Smriti

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
According to social law of ancient India, a
woman was always considered a minor. Divorce was
prohibited, although it sometimes took place. According
to Arthashastra, a wife who had been deserted by her
husband could seek a divorce.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
12. Which of the following Sultans in his farman
used to address the amirs as Masnad-i ali?
questions.explanation:
Bahlol Lodi in his farman used to address the
amirs as Masnad-i ali.
 He worked on Afghan theory of kingship regarded
himself as only ‘first among equals’, sat and ate with his
important nobles on the same carpet and called his
nobility Masnad-i-Ali.
Mushtaqi wrote, "He never sat on the throne and
forbade his nobles to remain standing before him.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
13. Who was the first president of the All India
trade Union Congress founded on 31 August
1920?
questions.explanation:
Lala Lajpat Rai was the first president of the
All India trade Union Congress founded on 31 August
1920.
 Deewan Chaman Lal was first general secretary of All
India trade union congress.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
15. 'The Sultan ordered the Maliks, Amirs, officers
of the court and persons of responsibility and
status not to go to each other's houses or to
collect parties at banquets; there were to be no
intermarriage among them unless the Sultan
had
been
informed
and
his
permission
obtained'. Identify the Sultan.
questions.explanation:
'The Sultan ordered the Maliks, Amirs,
officers of the court and persons of responsibility and
status not to go to each other's houses or to collect
parties at banquets; there were to be no intermarriage
among them unless the Sultan had been informed and
his permission obtained'. Sultan was Alauddin Khalji.
 Alauddin Khalji was greatest ruler of Khilji dynasty
and was first muslim ruler to extend his empire right up
to the extreme South of India.

metaphors) in Marathi bhakti poetry were

questions.explanation:
Poems classified as upadesha rupaka
(didactic metaphors) in Marathi bhakti poetry were
known as Bharud.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
19. In which of the following rulers' reigns the
bullion currency seems to have nearly entirely
replaced silver coinage?
questions.explanation:
In reign of Firuz Shah Tughlaq the bullion
currency seems to have nearly entirely replaced silver
coinage.
 Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced a token currency
system and minted vast quantities of new copper and
brass coins (tankas) that could be exchanged for fixed
amounts of gold and silver.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
20. Which of the following pairs indicate female
teachers according to ancient grammarians?
questions.explanation:
According to the ancient grammarians
Acharya and Upadhyaya indicate female teachers.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
21. Which of the following statement about
Chokhamela are correct?

(A)
Chokhamela was a Varkari Saint

(B)
His poems express devotion for Vitthal

(C)
As a great devotee of Vitthala, after his
death his samadhi was built inside the Vitthala
temple at Pandharpur

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (C) are correct about
Chokhamela. Chokhamela was saint in Maharashtra in
14th century. He wrote many Abhangas. He was varkari
saint. He was great devotee of Vithala, after his death
his samadhi was built inside the vithala temple of
Pandharpur.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
22. Who played an important role in distribution
of Gautama Buddha's sarira-dhatu (relics)
after his Mahaparinirvana?
questions.explanation:
Drona, a brahmin played an important role in
distribution of Gautam Buddha's Sarira Dhatu (relics)
after his mahaparinirvana Drona divided relics into ten
portions eight from the body relics, one from the Ashes
of Buddha's cremation pyre and one from the post used
to divide the relics.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
23. Who wrote the dictum: "all history is the
history of ideas".
questions.explanation:
Leo von Ranke wrote the dictum: "all history
is the history of ideas".
Leo von Ranke is german historian. His famous works
are "civil wars and monarchy in France in the sixteenth
and seventeenth centuries", history of the reformation in
Germany etc.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
24. Arrange the following landmark legal cases
chronologically starting from the earliest:

(A) Phulmony Case

(B) Vijialakshmi Case

(C) Maharaja Libel case

(D) Rukhmabai case

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Chronological order–
(A) Phulmony Case - 1862
(B) Vijialakshmi Case - 1881
(C) Maharaja Libel case - 1885
(D) Rukhmabai case - 1889-90

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
25. The first pilgrim centre for the Sikhs,
symbolized with the construction of a well with
84 steps, to reach the water for bathing, which
became sacred for the Sikhs was established by
which one of the following Sikh Gurus and at
which place?
questions.explanation:
The first pilgrim centre for the Sikhs,
symbolized with the construction of a well with 84
steps, to reach the water for bathing, which became
sacred for the Sikhs was established by Guru Amardas
at Goindwal.
 Goindwal is place where Guru Amardas met Guru
Ram Dasji the next guru. Guru Amardasji stayed 33
years in Goindwal.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
26. With regard to the Mughal finance system
which of the following statements are correct?

(A)
There was a well-developed system of
finance and credit in Mughal India

(B)
The use of hundis or bills of exchange
was widespread

(C)
There was no insurance system hence
risks of loss in transit were very high

(D)
Transport across land was itself costlier,
it was more vulnerable to the exactions of
chiefs and rebels

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (D) are correct
regarding Mughal finance system
(A) There was a well-developed system of finance and
credit in Mughal India.
(B) The use of hundis or bills of exchange was
widespread.
(D) Transport across land was itself costlier, it was
more vulnerable to the exactions of chiefs and rebels.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
27. Which of the following dynasties traced its
origin from Asura Naraka?

(A)
Bhanjas of Orissa

(B)
Palas of Bengal

(C)
Sailodbhavas of Orissa

(D)
Varmanas of Assam

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Varmanas of Assam traced its origin from
Asura Naraka.
Varman
dynasty
of
Assam
was
founded
by
Pushyavarman
contemporary
of
Samudragupta.
Bhaskaravarman claims that he was a descendant of
Narakasur, Bhagadatta and Vajradatta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
28. Arrange the following Gurjara Pratihara kings
in chronological order:

(A)
Mahendrapala - I

(B)
Mihirabhoja

(C)
Nagabhatta - II

(D)
Vatsaraja

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Chronological order of Gurjara Pratihara
kings–
(D) Vatsaraja (780-800 AD)
(C) Nagabhatta - II (800-833 AD)
(B) Mihirabhoja (836-885 AD)
(A) Mahendrapala - I (885-910)
 Founder of Gurjara Pratihara dynasty was Nagbatta I
(730-760 AD).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
29. Which of the following statements are true
about colonial cities?

(A)
Delhi, Agra and Lahore lost much of
their older glory

(B)
Dacca, Murshidabad and Patna came
into prominence in the British period

(C)
The Victoria terminal station of Bombay
was built after Mughal architectural style

(D)
According to C.A. Bayly, there was a
significant expansion of small towns in the mid-
Ganga region from around the 1720s

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) and (D) are correct about
colonial cities that
 Delhi, Agra and Lahore lost much of their older glory.
 According to C.A. Bayly, there was a significant
expansion of small towns in the mid-Ganga region from
around the 1720s.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
30. Which Sikh patriot was tried and executed by
the British Government in 1940 for the murder
of Sir Michael O'Dwyer, who was involved in
the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation:
Sardar Udham Singh was tried and executed
by the British Government in 1940 for the murder of Sir
Michael O'Dwyer, who was involved in the infamous
Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 Udham Singh killed Michael O' Dwyer on 13 March
1940.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
31. The earliest extant examples of the Mughal
baluster columns are found solely in which of
the following Mughal emperor's fortress
palaces?
questions.explanation:
The earliest extant examples of the Mughal
baluster columns are found solely in Shahjahan's
fortress palaces of Agra, Lahore and Delhi.
 Baldachin of Machchhi Bhawan and zanana mina
bazar both in Agra fort seem to be first functional
columns with a baluster shape in Mughal architecture.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
32. Which of the following are included among the
seven limbs of ancient Indian State?

(A) Svamin
(B) Amatya

(C) Janapada
(D) Yuvaraja

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Saptanga theory of state was given by
Kautilya in Arthasashtra. The seven limbs of state are
King, Amatya, Janapada, Durga (fort), Kosa (treasure)
Danda and Mitra.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
33. Which of the following texts were authored by
the Kashmiri poet Kshemendra?

(A) Kuttanimata

(B) Kalavilasa

(C) Prabodhachandrodaya

(D) Samayamatrika

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Kalavilasa and Samayamatrika were authored
by the Kashmiri poet Kshemendra.
He also composed Ramayanamanjari, Bharat Manjari,
Brihatkathamanjari. In poetics he wrote Auchitya
Vichar Charcha, Kavikanthabharana and Suvrittatilaka.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
34. Which female social reformer wrote the short
stories
–
Sultana's
Dream
(1905)
and
Avarodhbasini (1929), criticizing the custom of
purdah among Muslims?
questions.explanation:
Begam Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain a feminist
from Bengal wrote the short stories - Sultana's Dream
(1905) and Avarodhbasini (1929), criticizing the custom
of purdah among Muslims.
 In 1916 Rokeya founded Muslim women's association
an organization that fought for women's education and
employment.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
35. During the Saka-Satavahana period the range
of interest on fixed deposit (akshayanivi) as
described in the inscription of Nasik Cave No.
10 was:
questions.explanation:
During the Saka-Satavahana period the range
of interest on fixed deposit (akshayanivi) as described in
the inscription of Nasik Cave No. 10 was from 9 to
12%.
 The Nasik Cave No. 10 is known as "Nahapana
Vihara" Cave No. 10 is the second largest Vihara and
contains six inscriptions of the family of Nahapana. The
inscriptions of Cave No. 10 reveals that in 105-106 CE
western satraps defeated satavahanas.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
36. Which of the following Sailendra rulers are
known to have had friendly relations with their
contemporary Indian kings?

(A)
Samaragravira

(B)
Balaputradeva

(C)
Chudamanivarman

(D)
Sri-Maravijayottungavarman

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Sailendra rulers like Balaputradeva,
Chudamanivarman and Sri-Maravijayottungavarman
are known to have friendly relations with their
contemporary Indian kings.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:

the

given below:
questions.explanation:
Chronological order of organizations
All India Trade Union Congress -1920
Hindustan Socialist Republican Association -1928
Independent Labour Party of India (Dr. Ambedkar) -
1936
Indian National Trade Union Congress
-1947

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
38. Which of the following suttas are associated
with the Dighanikaya?

(A) Brahmajala Sutta

(B) Mahapadana Sutta

(C) Mahaparinibbana Sutta

(D) Samannaphala Sutta

Choose the correct answer form the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
All of the Suttas given in options are
associated with digha nikaya.
(A) Brahmajala Sutta - mainly concerned with 62 types
of wrong views.
(B) Samannaphala Sutta
- The
fruits of
the
contemplative life.
(C) Mahapadana Sutta - Tells the story of past Buddha
up to shortly after his englightenment, the story is
similar to that of Gautam Buddha.
(D) Mahaparinibbana Sutta - Story of the last few
months of the Buddha's life, his death and funeral and
the distribution of his relics.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
39. From
among
the
following
statements
regarding Munshi Premchand and his works,
which of them are correct?

(A) Premchand was among the first to portray
the Dalits as independent and recognizable
characters both as part of the poor and with
their own particular problems

(B) Premchand was extremely insensitive to
the political and social movements of his times

(C) Premchand was concerned both about
social evils and enslaved conditions of his
country

(D) One of his (Premchand's) last and most
famous stories, Kafan (the Shroud), was first
published in Hindi in 1935 and later appeared
in Urdu

Choose the correct answer from the option
given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) and (C) are correct regarding
Munshi Premchand and his works
(A) Premchand was among the first to portray the Dalits
as independent and recognizable characters both as part
of the poor and with their own particular problems.
(C) Premchand was concerned both about social evils
and enslaved conditions of his country.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
40. "At some times and places there will be no
roads, docks, harbours, canals, works of
irrigation, hospitals, schools, colleges, printing
presses, unless the government establishes
them".

The above quotation from John Stuart Mill's
Political Economy refers to which policy
adopted by the Company government?
questions.explanation:
The above quotation from John Stuart mill's
political economy refers to policy of interventionism
adopted by the company government.
 John Stuart mill was utilitarian. He gave theory of
liberty.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
41. Ibn Battuta informs that the Sultan had fixed
Wednesday for freeing male slaves, Friday for
freeing female slaves and Saturday for
marrying men slaves to female slaves. Identify
the Sultan.
questions.explanation:
Ibn Battuta informs about Muhammad Bin
Tughlaq that the Sultan had fixed Wednesday for
freeing male slaves, Friday for freeing female slaves
and Saturday for marrying men slaves to female slaves.
 Muhammad Bin Tughlaq ruled from 1324 to 1351.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
42. Which of the following statements regarding
Gandhi's concept of Satyagraha are correct?

(A)
For
Gandhi,
Satyagraha
aimed
to
penetrate the barriers of prejudice. ill-will,
dogmatism, self-righteousness and selfishness

(B)
Gandhi explained the effectiveness of
Satyagraha in terms of the spiritual impact of
suffering love

(C)
The Satyagraha was considered by
Gandhi as the ultimate tool of humiliating the
opponent

(D)
Gandhi's political realism triumphed
over his moral idealism and despite its claims
to the contrary, his Satyagrahas were not
always purely spiritual in nature

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and D are correct
regarding Gandhi’s concept of satyagraha. For Gandhi
satyagraha aimed to penetrate barriers of prejudice ill
will, dogmatism, self righteousness and selfishness.
Gandhi explained the effectiveness of Satyagraha in
terms of the spiritual impact of suffering love. Gandhi’s
political realism triumphed over his moral idealism and
despite its claims to the contrary his satyagrahas were
not always purely spiritual in nature.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:

Balban's theory of kingship are correct?

(A)
Kingship is the vice-regency of God on
earth. The king is the shadow of God

(B)
External dignity and prestige were not
considered as essential for Kingship

(C)

Balban believed that Persian customs
and ways of life are not necessary to emulate

given below:

Balban's theory of kingship.

king is the shadow of God.
(C) A distinction between the high-born and the low-
born was constantly emphasized by Balban.

the highest punishment?
questions.explanation:

to Varna. According to Manu a brahmana was to be

varnas for the offence of theft.

in the history of the Delhi Sultanate, decided a
succession issue on their own initiative.

strength

(B) She gave her accession the form of a
contract when she asked people of depose her if
she did not fulfil their expectations

(C) It shows the robustness of the Turkish
mind in accepting a woman as ruler
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (C) are correct about
Razia's accession to the throne of Delhi.
 Razia Sultan ruled from 1236-40.
 Razia gave up Purdah and started wearing Kuba (coat)
and kulah (cap) like men.

questions.explanation:

was also known as Lakhbakhsh.
Qutbuddin Aibak was general of Muhammad Ghori. He
was in charge of the Ghurid territories in northern India
and after Muhammad Ghoris's death. He became the
ruler of independend kingdom.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
76. Who was the first elected president of the All
India Depressed Classes Association formed in
1926?
questions.explanation:
Rao Bahadur M. C. Rajah was the first
elected president of the All India Depressed Classes
Association formed in 1926.
 M. C. Rajah was leader of justice party.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
77. In the Bayana Hoard, coins of which Gupta
ruler have been found in the highest number?
questions.explanation:
In the Bayana Hoard, coins of Chandragupta
II have been found in the highest number among the
gupta kings. Kumargupta I issued the largest varities of
coins. His 628 coins in the Bayana hoard belong to 14
different types.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
78. Given below are two statements:

Statement (I) : When a soldier died showing
exemplary valour while fighting for the king,
he was granted land for the livelihood of his
dependents, called 'Mrityukavritti'.

Statement (II) : A Chandella inscription
records the grant of such a 'Mrityukavritti'.

In the light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below:
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement (I) is true that when a soldier died
showing exemplary valour while fighting for the king,
he was granted land for the livelihood of his
dependents, called 'Mrityukarvritti'.
Statement (II) is true that a Chandella inscription
records the grant of such a 'Mrityukavritti'.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
79. Who among the following travellers visited a
"Hospitol of Birds" at Cambay in 1623-24,
where he saw some lame, sick and mateless
birds and some tiny orphan mice. He writes,
"A venerable old man with a white beard was
keeping them in a box amongst cotton, with his
spectacles on his nose, giving them milk to eat
with a bird's feather, because they were so little
that as yet they could eat nothing else, and as
he told us, he intended when they are grown up
to let them go free whither they please".
questions.explanation:
Pietro Della Valle visited a "Hospitol of
Birds" at Cambay in 1623-24.
 Pietro Della Valle the famous Italian traveller came in
India during reign of Jahangir. He visited Surat.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
80. In Which of the following texts are the Sabha
and the Samiti mentioned as the two daughters'
of a Vedic deity?
questions.explanation:
In Atharvaveda sabha and samiti mentioned
as two daughter's of vedic diety.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 81. Isvarakrishna was:
questions.optionA:
a Vaishnava teacher from early medieval
Orissa
questions.optionB: a King of Assam in the eighth century AD
questions.optionC:
a philosopher of one of the six systems of
philosophy
questions.optionD: a lawgiver of the medieval period

six systems of philosophy. Isvarakrishna composed
Samkhyakarika which is the earliest surviving text of
samkhya school of Indian philosophy. In the text author
described himself as a successor of the disciples from
the great sage kapila.
