questions.questionText:
83. Which one of the following statements is true
about the stand of the communist party of
India during the India-China war of 1962?
questions.optionA:
One wing of the party supported the Indian
Government against the Chinese attack
questions.optionB:
The Communist Party (Marxist) wing of the
party supported the stand of China
questions.optionC:
One wing of the party criticized China as a
bourgeois state
questions.optionD:
The Communist Party (Marxist) wing joined
hands with the revolutionary elements across
the globe
questions.explanation:
Statement (1) is true about the stand of the
communist party of India during the India-China war of
1962 that one wing of the party supported the Indian
Government against the Chinese attack.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
84. Which of the following cave temples of Ellora
are related to Brahmanical religion?

(A) Dhumera Lena

(B) Indra-Sabha

(C) Jagannatha Sabha

(D) Ravana Ki Khai

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Dhumera Lena and Ravan ki Khai (Cave-14)
of Ellora are related to Brahmanical religion.
 Ellora caves contain 17 Hindu caves (13 to 29) 12
buddhist caves and 5 jain caves.
Some famous Hindu cave temples of Ellora are
Rameshwar temple (Cave 21), Kailash temple (Cave
16), The Dashavatara (Cave 15) and Nilkantha (Cave
22).

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
85. Who among the following kings mentioned in
the Rajatarangini personally went to a leather
worker (charmakara) with a request to get a
small piece of land of his cottage needed for the
construction of temple of Tribhuvanasvami?
questions.explanation:
King Chandrapida mentioned in the
Rajatarangini personally went to a leather worker
(charmakara) with a request to get a small piece of land
of his cottage needed for the construction of temple of
Tribhuvanasvami temple.
 Avantivarman was founder of utpala dynasty.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
86. On 27th December 1891, which socio-religious
reform movement met for its first general
gathering in Qadiyan, Punjab?
questions.explanation:
On 27th December 1891, Ahmadiya socio-
religious reform movement held first general gathering
in Qadiyan Punjab.
 Ahmadiya is the third most popular branch of Islam
which originated from India and spread all across
world. It was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in
1889.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
87. Which one of the following statements in not
true?
questions.optionA:
Annie Besant of the Madras Theosophical
society asserted that in ancient times Hindu
women were educated and moved freely in
society
questions.optionB:
The Arya Samaj of North India strongly
supported the cause of female education
questions.optionC:
The Hunter Commission Report of 1882
recommended more liberal grants-in-aid for
girls' schools than for boys' and special
scholarships and prizes for girls
questions.optionD:
Dhondo Keshav Karve was against the
education of high-caste Hindu widows
questions.explanation:
Statement (4) is not true that Dhondo Keshav
Karve was against the education of high-caste Hindu
widows.
 D.K. Karve was a social reformer in India in the field
of women welfare. He advocated widow remarriage and
he himself married widow. Karve was pioneer in
promoting widow's education. He founded first
women's university in India SNDT women's university.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
88. Who founded the autonomous kingdom of
Hyderabad in1724?
questions.explanation:
Asaf Jaah was the founder of autonomous
kingdom of Hyderabad. He is also known as Nijam-ul-
Mulk. He was intermittently viceroy of Deccan under
the Mughal emperors from 1713 to 1721.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
89. Which of the following statements regarding
interpretation in historical writing are correct?

(A) Interpretation as an essential step in
historical method seems to lie beyond criticism
and exposition

(B) To know what a document means is as
much a challenge to critical judgment as to
know when or by whom was it written, or
whether one may trust it

(C) The literary exposition of historical data is
greatly conditioned by the interpretation one
places upon them

(D) Factual interpretation deals with the facts
of a document, not with the words

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
questions.explanation:
Statements (B), (C) and (D) are correct
regarding interpretation in historical writing.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
90. took keen interest in debates, and when
Srinatha defeated his court poet, Dindima, in a
disputation, he honoured the former with the
title of Kavi Sarvabhauma, and 'bathed him in
gold coins'. Identify this Vijayanagar ruler:
questions.explanation:
He took keen interest in debates, and when
Srinatha defeated his court poet, Dindima, in a
disputation, he honoured the former with the title of
Kavi Sarvabhauma, and 'bathed him in gold coins'. The
ruler was Devaraya II .
 Devaraya II was greatest ruler of sangama dynasty.
 He inducted muslim archers into army.
 He was first Vijayanagar ruler to collect tribute from
ceylone.
 Abul Razzaq visited during rule of Devaraya II.
Direction (91-95):
Read the following passage
and answer the question given below:

Ancient India has bequeathed to us a vast
treasury
of
texts
which
represent
the
intellectual and literary activities of more than
two thousand years and cover a wide fields.
The earliest literary work, the Samhita of the
Rigveda, is at least three thousand years old
and may be even considerably older. A
continuous stream of literature flowing since
that remote age, widening in course of
centuries and embracing almost all fields of
human endeavour excepting political activity
throws a light on the civilization of India such
as we do not meet with in cases of other ancient
cultures. This mass of literature deal with
philosophy and religion, including ethics, ritual
and
ceremonial;
cosmogony,
cosmology,
geography, astronomy and the allied sciences;
political and economic doctrines and practices;
and in a minor way, with almost all branches of
secular life. It includes, besides a mass of
religious texts, purely literary works such as
epics, lyrics, kavyas (poems), dramas and prose
romances, as well as biographies and folk tales.
This literature is as bulky in volume as it is
varied in its contents. Although it does not help
us very much in reconstructing the political
history of ancient India, it throws a flood of
light on an enables us to trace the various
stages in the development of culture and
civilization in ancient India, such as is not
possible in the case of ancient Egypt, Western
Asia and China and even Greece and Rome.

fold,
individuals

stream.

stream

Read the following passage
and answer the question given below

The Indian National Congress, being a
movement and not just a party, included within
its
fold,
individuals
and
groups
which
subscribed to widely divergent political and
ideological perspectives. It was the mainstream
organization
but
not
the
only
stream.
Obviously, the non-Congress movements were
never seen as parallel streams, as some have
maintained. Though they were outside the
Congress, most of them were not really
separate from it and at no stage they became
alternatives to the Congress. The only ones
which may be said to have formed of an
alternative
stream
of
politics
were
the
communal and casteist movements which were
not
national
or
anti-imperialist.
Several
Satyagraha
campaigns
–
apart
from
innumerable mass agitational campaigns –
were waged between 1919 and 1942. The
movement in its various forms and phases took
modern politics to the people. It did not appeal
to their pre-modern consciousness based on
religion, caste and locality or loyalty to the
traditional rulers. Though in some cases caste
structure was used in villages to enforce
discipline in a movement whose motivation and
demands had nothing to do with caste. The
social and religious reform movements which
developed during the 19th century as part of the
defence against colonialization of Indian
culture merged with the national movement. A
a mass movement, while the Indian national
movement was able to tap the diverse energies,
talents and capacities of a large varieties of
people to fight against the British rule,
emphasis was also laid on the constructive
programme.

98. Which kind of individuals were not associated
with the Indian national movement?
questions.explanation:
Imperialists were not associated with the
Indian national movement. Imperialists supported
British.

questions.questionText:
1.
What is the nature to the evidence for
associating
Chandragupta
Maurya
with
Bhadrabahu?
(1) Numismatic
(2) Epigraphic
(2) Chinese testimony
(4) Early historic

iconographic
questions.explanation:
Nature of the evidence is epigraphic for
associating Chandragupta Maurya with Bhadrabahu.
 Brihatkathakosa describes the legend of Bhadrabahu
and mentions Chandragupta in its 131st story.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
2.
The technique Siyahi qalam or nim qalam was
brought to India by the painters from which of
the following regions?
(1) Arabia

(2) Persia
(3) Transoxiana
(4) Turkey
questions.explanation:
The technique siyahi qalam or nim qalam was
brought to India by the painters from Persia. This is
technique of fine brush drawing with black ink that
developed in persia in 15th century. This technique also
admired by Jahangir.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
4.
Who wrote the seminal work-Stree-Purush-
Tulana [A Comparison between Women and
Men] in 1882?
(1) Kashibai Kanitkar (2) Anandibai Karve
(3) Ramabai Ranade
(4) Tarabai Shinde
questions.explanation:
The seminal work - stree purush Tulana
(comparison between women and men) in 1882 was
written by Tarabai Shinde.
Shinde was feminist writer from Berar province of
Buldhana (present Maharashtra) who protested against
upper caste patriarchy and the caste system in India. She
was also member of Satyasodhak samaj. The pamphlet
stree purush Tulana was originally published in
Marathi.
 Kashibai Kanitkar was first major woman writer from
Maharashtra. Her famous novels are Ranga Rao and
Palakhicha Gonda.
 Ramabai Ranade started "Hindu Ladies social club' in
Mumbai to develop public speaking among woman.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
5.
From
among
the
following
statements
regarding Non-Cooperation movement, which
are correct?

(A) Under the Non-Cooperation, Gandhi urged
the people not to cooperate with an unjust and
hence evil system

(B)
By
describing
the
British
India
administrative system as an evil, Gandhi
removed the spell of fear of the “terror of law”
from the hearts of the people

(C) Under Non-Cooperation Gandhi urged the
people to break the civil and criminal law

(D) Gandhi urged the people to fearlessly go to
prisons, which he termed as „His Majesty‟s
Hotel‟

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
(1) (A) and (C) only
(2) (B), (C) and (D) only
(3) (A), (B) and (D) only
(4) (C) and (D) only
questions.explanation:
Statement A, B and C are correct regarding
non co-operation movement.
(A) Under the non co-operation Gandhi urged the
people not to co-operate with an unjust and hence evils.
(B) By describing the British Indian administrative
system as an evil. Gandhi removed the spell of fear of
the "terror of law" from the hearts of people.
(D) Gandhi urged the people to fearlessly go to prisons,
which he termed as "His majesty's hotel".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
6.
On the island of Java in Southeast Asia,

(A) The first Indian settlements were set up in
the first century AD

(B) Indian political power was however
established only in the third century AD

(C) According to a Buddhist traveler, it was
brahmanical religion that was prevalent in the
fifth century AD

(D) The Pallavas had established their
suzerainty by the fourth century AD
[Exam Date: 29.11.2021] Shift-II

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(1) (A), (B) and (C) only
(2) (A) and (C) only
(3) (B), (C) and (D) only
(4) (B) and (C) only
questions.explanation:
On the island of Java in south-east asia option
(A) and (C) are correct.
(A) The first Indian settlements were set up in the first
century AD.
(C) According to a Buddhist traveler, it was
brahmanical religion that was prevalent in the fifth
century AD.
Java Island–The site of Trinil on java is famous for the
discovery of fossilized remains of Homo erectus in
1891. The Mataram Kingdom (8th century C.E.) centred
in south central java ruled by Shailendra dynasty. Later
kings of Mataram Kingdom accepted Mahayana
buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
7. The city of Burhanpur was established by
Nasir Khan of

(1) Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh

(2) Qutb Shan dynasty of Golcinda

(3) Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur

(4) Imad Shahi dynasty of Bidar
questions.explanation:
Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh. Burhanpur was
founded in 1399 by Nasir Khan the first independent
prince of the Faruqi dynasty of Khandesh and it was
annexed by the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1601. The
city with its wall and massive gates, served as the
Deccan headquarters of Mughals until Aurangzeb
moved the capital to Aurangabad in 1636.

questions.questionText:
8.
Which of the following crops do not find
mention in the Ain-i Akbari in any of the
dastur circles?

(A) Coffee

(B) Tea

(C) Opium

(D) Indigo

(E) Tobacco

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(1) (A), (B) and (C) only
(2) (B), (C) and (D) only
(3) (A), (C) and (E) only
(4) (A), (B) and (E) only
questions.explanation:
Coffee, opium and Tobacco do not find
mention in the Ain-i-Akbari in any of the dastur circle.
 Ain-i-Akbari is a 16th century detailed document
recording the administration of the mughal empire
under emperor Akbar written by his court historian
Abul Fazl in the persian language.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
9. Which of the following statements are true
about Panchsheel?

(A) Nehru used the term in honour of the US
President in September 1954.

(B)
The
Panchsheel
principles
were
incorporated in a United Nations General
Assembly resolution presented
by India,
Yugoslavia and Sweden.

(C) Burma and Indonesia did not support the
idea of Panchsheel.

(D) The policy of Non-alignment is a direct
consequence of the principles of Panchsheel.

(E) Nehru and the Chinese Premier Chau-En –
Lai signed the Panchsheel agreement in 1954.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
(1) (A), (C) and (E) only
(2) (B), (D) and (E) only
(3) (A), (D) and (E) only
(4) (B) and (D)
questions.explanation:
(B) The Panchsheel principles were
incorporated in a United nations general assembly
resolution presents by India, Yugoslavia and Sweden.
(D) The policy of non-alignment is direct consequence
of the principles of panchsheel.
(E) Nehru and Chinese premier Chau-En-Lai signed the
panchsheel agreement in 1954.
Panchsheel principles–
(1) Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity
and sovereighty.
(2) Mutual non aggression
(3) Mutual non interference in each other internal affairs
(4) Equality and co-operation for mutual benefit.
(5) Peaceful co-existence.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
10. Regarding the protection of routes under
Mughal administration, which of the following
statements are correct ?

(A) The protection of the routes was regarded
as one of the foremost duties of the
administration

(B) The organisation of the carvans and serais
of the tandas of banjaras, who went armed, and
possibly of flotiallas in the rivers was mainly
assigned to meet the threat of robbery on the
routes

(C) Under Mughal empire, the officer in whose
jurisdiction robbery of theft occurred, had to
recover the goods or had to compensate the
victim himself

(D) The officers met this obligation by
pursuing a policy of ferocious reprisals and
sacking the suspected villages

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
(1) (A), (C) and (D) only
(2) (B) and (C) only
(3) (A), (B), (C) and (D)
(4) (B), (C) and (D) only
questions.explanation:
All statement given about mughal
administration are correct.
Protection of routes was duty of mughal administration.
Flotillas in the rivers was assigned to met the threats of
robbery on the routes. Under Mughal empire the officer
in whose jurisdiction robbery of theft occured had to
recover the goods or had to compensate the victim
himself. The officers met this obligation by pursuing a
policy of ferocious reprisals and sacking the suspected
village.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
13. Who started Rajamundry Social Reform
Association in 1878?
(1) Rama Iyengar

(2) Sesha Iyengar
(3) K. Viresalingam Pantalu
(4) Rubgundai Raghunath Rao
questions.explanation:
Rajamundry Social Reform Association was
founded by K. Viresalingam Pantalu. Through this
association, he fought against hiring nautch girls and
spearheaded a campaign for widow remarriage, on
December 11, 1881 he organized first widow
remarriage in the country.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
14. Pratimoksha meant
(1) The negation of salvation
(2) a materialist doctrine of the Charvakas
(3) monastic rules of the Buddhist order
(4) a religious functionary of the Jainas.
questions.explanation:
Pratimoksha meant monastic rules of the
Buddhist order. Pratimoksha is the basic code of
monastic discipline consisting of 227 rules for fully
ordained
morks (bhikkhus) and 311 for nuns
(bhikkhunis). It is contained in the Suttavibhanga, a
division of the Vinaya pitaka.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II

who were known as the authors of inscriptions:
(A) Harishena
(B) Ravikirti
(C) Ravishanti
(D) Vatsabhatti

given below:
(1) (A), (D), (C), (B)
(2) (A), (B), (C), (D)
(3) (B), (C), (A), (D)
(4) (D), (A), (B), (C)
questions.explanation:
Chronological order–
(A) Harishena - court poet of Samudragupta wrote
Prayag Prashasti
(D) Vatsabhatti - composed mandasur inscription, court
poet of Kumaragupta
(C) Ravishanti - In gupta age after Kumargupta.
(B) Ravikirti - composed meguti inscription of
Pulakeshin. He mentioned defeat of Harsha by
Ravikirti.

17. The story of Sunahsepa in which a father is
described as selling his son occure in
(1) Aitareya Brahmana
(2) Satpatha Brahmana
(3) Taittiriya Brahmana
(4) Tandya Brahmana
questions.explanation:
The story of Sunahsepa in which a father is
described as selling his son occurs in Aitareya
Brahmana.
 Aitareya Brahmana is Brahman text of Rigveda in this
text there is mention of rituals in throne getting
ceremony.
 Satapath Brahman mentions kings as Gandhar,
Shalya, Kekaya, Kuru, Panchala, etc.
 Taittiriya brahman is brahman text of Yajurveda.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
18. The Hyderabadi administrative system in the
late eighteenth century can be identified as a
„patron-client relationship‟, because,
(1) The Nizam displayed his allegiance to the
Mughal Emperor and regularly paid
tributes
(2) The local Hindu landowners were subdued
by the Nizam and they were forced to pay
him tributes
(3) The
semi-autonomous
rulers
of
the
Hyderabad state were allowed to govern on
their own in return for an annual tribute to
the Nizam and the Mughals
questions.explanation:
The Hyderabadi administrative system in the
late eighteenth century can be identified as a „patron-
client relationship‟, because The Nizam displayed his
allegiance to the Mughal Emperor and regularly paid
tributes.
 Mir Osman Ali Khan was last Nizam of Hyderabad.
He deposed from power in 1948 in operation polo.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
19. The Seventh Pillar Edict of King Asoka occurs
on
(A) Delhi – Meerut Pillar
(B) Delhi – Topra Pillar
(C) Sarnath Pillar
(D) Lauriya – Araraj Pillar

Choose the correct answer form the options
given below:
(1) (B) and (D) only
(2) (A), (C) and (D) only
(3) (B) only
(4) (D) only
questions.explanation:
The Seventh Pillar Edict of King Asoka
occurs on Delhi Topra Pillar. Pillar edict VII mentions
works done by Ashoka for Dhamma policy. He says
that all sects desire both self control and purity of mind.
 Capital of Sarnath pillar is national amblem of India.
 Lauriya Araraj pillar - Bihar, pillar bear six edicts of
Ashoka.
 Delhi Meerut pillar - This pillar brought to Delhi from
Meerut by Firoze Shah Tughlaq.

of early India?

Aiyadigal Kadavarkon
(A) Tirumular
(B) Tirumangai
(C) Tirumalisai

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below:
questions.explanation:
Aiyadigal Kadavarkon and Tirumular are
well known saivas of early India.
 Aiyadigal Kadavarkon, was a ruler of Kadava dynasty
and was ruling from kanchipuram later he became the
46th Nayanar saint in Tamil Nadu.
 Tirumular was a Tamil shaivite mystic and writer.
Tirumurai was main work of Tirumular.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2020/June 2021 (29.11.2021-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
22. Regarding Dabistan-I Mazahib, which of the
following statements are correct ?
(A) The Dabistan-i Mazahib refers to the
compositions of Guru Nanak as replete
with
praises
of
God
and
ethical
instructions
(B) The author of Dabistan refers to the Adi
Granth compiled by Guru Arjan
(C) The author of Dabistan refers to the
practice of Sikhs to request the entire
congregation to pray for the fulfillment of
an individual‟s wish
(D) The Dabistan contains extremely useful
information on the organization of the Sikh
community

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below:
(1) (A), (B) and (C) only
(2) (B) and (C) only
(3) (A), (C) and (D) only
(4) (B) and (D) only
questions.explanation:
Regarding Dabistan-I Mazahib statement (A),
(C) and (D) are correct. Dabistan-I Mazahib, a
seventeenth century work in persian, is a unique study
of different religious creeds and systems, including
early Sikhism. The work is attributed by scholars to an

contemporary writer.

the neighbourhood.

correct answer from the options given below:

true.
(2) Both Statement I and Statement II are
false.
(3) Statement I is true but Statement II is
false.

introspection about indigenous culture and institutions.

century India was occasioned by the colonial presence,

in the progress of society: If religion did not keep pace
with the demands of time, it would get fossilized.

The state policy under Akbar from 1560
onwards, roughly down to 1575, had thus often

years as their main potential opponents among
the nobles or ashraf among the Muslim
population.

Direction (96-100)

Read the following passage and answer the
question given below :

Indian National Movement was most firmly
and deeply rooted in an understanding of the
nature and character of colonial economic
domination and exploitation. Three names
stand out who carried out the economic
analysis of British rule during 1870-1905, i.e.
Dadabhai Naoroji, the Grand Old Man of
India, Justice MG Ranade and Romesh
Chandra Dutt, a retired civil servant. These
three leaders along with G.V. Joshi. G.K.
Gokhale,
G.
Subramaniya
Iyer,
Prithws
Chandra Ray and a host of others raised basic
questions regarding the nature and purpose of
British rule. For them, the essence of British
imperialism lay in the subordination of the
Indian economy to the British economy. They
were able to see that colonialism no longer
functioned through crude tools of plunder and
tribute and mercantilism but operated through
the disguised and complex mechanism of free
trade and foreign capital investment, by
transforming India into a supplier of food
stuffs and raw material to the metropolis and
making India a market for the metropolitan
manufacturers. Ever since the 1840s, the
British economists, officials had seen the
investment of foreign capital, along with law
and order, as the major instrument for the
development of India, an argument the early
Indian nationalists vehemently refuted. They
argued that instead of encouraging and
augmenting Indian capital, foreign capital
replaced and suppressed it which led to the
drain of capital from India and further
strengthed the British hold over the Indian
economy. They also highlighted the progressive
decline
and
ruin
of
India's
traditional
handicrafts
in
the
interest
of
British
manufacturers. The political consequences of
such policies were no less harmful and which
led to India's political subjugation.

Budhha stress the need to protect cow
questions.explanation:

- Suttanipata.
The Abhidhamma Pitaka is a detailed scholastic
analysis and summary of the Buddha's teachings in the
Suttas. Here the Suttas are reworked into a schematized
system of general principles that might be called

questions.questionText:
11. Which one of these is/are correct out of the
following :

(A) Aurobindo Ghosh wrote 'New lamps for Old'

(B) New Lamps for Old described the Congress
as being out of contact with the 'Proletariat'

(C) New Lamps for Old' characterised Congress
as unnational

(D) Aurobindo Ghosh thought that the Congress
was 'dying of consumption'

(E) Ranade wrote 'Essays in European Economics'

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
option given below:
questions.explanation:
The book "New lamps for Old" was written
by Shri Aurobindo Ghosh and was published in 1893.
He was a philosopher, Yogi, guru, poet and nationalist
of India The "New lamps for Old" was a series of
articles (1893-1894) that simply criticized the Congress
for being out of touch with the 'proletariat'. From the
book New lamps for Old, according to author - If the
Congress cannot really face the light of a free and
serious criticism, then the sooner it hides its face the
better. So, it characterized Congress as unnational.
Also, Aurobindo Ghosh thought that the Congress was
'dying of consumption.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2021/June 2022 (10.10.2022-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
12. Given below are two statements:
Statement (I) :
The Harappans did not believe
in animism
Statement (II) : No temples have been found at
any Harappan sites

In the light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.optionC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.optionD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement (I) is false, but statement (II) is
true.
Even though no temples or religious structures have
been found from the Indus Valley, their society was not
atheistic. They believed in life after death. They accept
the existence of God. The Mother - goddess was the
most venerated god. Animals were worshipped too.
Pipal and Neem trees were also worshipped and have
been found engraved on seals in large numbers. Also,
Harrapans had many superstitions. They believed that
ghosts and evil spirits were capable of harming them,
and therefore, they used amulets against them.

priest, a high caste or a slave was a Paika. The Paikas
were organized into a four - member groups called
Gots.
 Each member was jointly responsible for military
service for at least 12 months.

given below :
questions.explanation:

The Kuka movement marked the first major reaction of
the people in the Punjab to the new political order
initiated by the British after 1849.
Surendra Nath Banerji was disqualified for the I.C.S.
Exam in 1869.
The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was established on 2nd
April 1870 at Poona.
Sisir Kumar Ghosh (1840-1911) started the Indian
league in 25 September, 1875 with the object of
stimulating the sense of nationalism amongst the
people. Swami Dayanand Saraswati laid the foundation
of the Arya Samaj at Bombay on 10th April 1875.

(B) Pancha-mandli

(C) Ashtakula-adhikarana

(D) Sabhamandala

(E) Tri-mandli

administrative system at the village level. The
Damodarpur copper plate of the reign of Budhagupta
mentions a Ashtakula Adhikarana (a board of eight
members) headed by Mahattara. The sanchi inscription
of the time of Chandragupta II mentions the pancha-
mandali which may have been corporate body.

Shall we ostrich-like bury our head and ignore this
original contemporary material in the Marathi language
and base our conclusions on writing, of distant British
and Dutch merchants whose trade was thrown in
confusion by Shivaji's revolt for the Liberation of his

Maratha administration as it obtained in the homeland.

School postulates and cultivate a correct perspective.

Reason R : Raja Ram Mohan Rai wrote the
Precepts of Jesus, published in 1820

In light of the above statements choose the most
appropriate answer from the options given
below
questions.optionA:
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct
explanation of A
questions.optionB:
Both A and R are correct but R is not the
correct explanation of A
questions.optionC: A is correct but R is not correct
questions.optionD: A is not correct but R is correct
questions.explanation:
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A).
From the given two statements-
Assertion (A) : It is a correct statement that- Raja Ram
Mohan Rai has rejected Christianity and has denied the
divinity of Jesus-Christ.
Reason (R) : Raja Ram Mohan Rai has wrote the book-
Precepts of Jesus, which was published in 1820.
 [Both statements (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the
correct explanation of (A)]
 Some other literary works of Raja Ram mohan Ray
are Tuhfat-ul-muwahiddin, Bengali grammar, The
universal religion and Gaudiya vyakaran.
[Exam Date: 10.10.2022] Shift-II

questions.questionText:
6.

the
22nd
Tirthankara,
was
associated with :
questions.explanation:
Neminath lived 81,000 years before the 23rd
Jain Tirthankara-Parshvanatha. He was the only child of
king Samudravijaya and queen Shivadevi. 'Krishna' who
was the 9th and last Jain Vasudeva, was his first cousin.
So, 'Neminath' the 22nd Tirthankara was associated with
'Krishna'.

questions.questionText:
8.
Who took up to issue of cow protection in
1871?
questions.explanation:
Kukas- In the 1870's the Namdhari Sikhs
were the first to start a Cow protection revolution, the
Kuka Revolution, in which they revolted against the
Britishers in support of protection of the Cow, in the
process sacrificing their own lives.
Kuka rebellion was led by Balak singh and his follower
Guru Ramsingh. During kuka rebellion viceroy of India
was Lord Northbrook.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2021/June 2022 (10.10.2022-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
9. Who among the following rued the destruction
of Kashmir under Sikandar?
questions.explanation:
Jonaraja rued the destruction of Kashmir
under Sikandar. Sikandar shah miri was sixth sultan of
shah miri dynasty of Kashmir and remembered for
Strenous efforts to convert the Hindus of Kashmir to
Islam. These efforts included destruction of numerous
old temples, prohibition of Hindu rites and festivals. He
is known as "Butcher of Kashmir".

civilization depicts a tree holding a fish and a
fox-like animal below reflecting the story of
'The
Clever
Fox'
narrated
in
the
Panchtanatra?
questions.explanation:
From the Harrapan civilization site of 'Lothal'
(Lothal- was one of the Southernmost sites of the
ancient Indus Valley civilization, located in the region
of the modern state of Gujarat); the painted pot was
found which depicts a tree holding a fish and a fox-like
animal below reflecting the story of 'The Clever Fox'
narrated in the Panchatantra.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2021/June 2022 (10.10.2022-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
11. Daojali Hading, a Neolithic site is located in
which area?
questions.explanation:
'Daojali Hading', is a Neolithic site which is
located in the 'North Cachar Hills' of 'Dima Hasao'-
district of Assam, India. It is first stratified neolithic site
discovered in northeast India. The cord marked pottery
is a unique characteristic of this site.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2021/June 2022 (10.10.2022-II) Paper II
questions.questionText:
12. Which among the following Mughal painters
drew the portrait of the shah of Persia?
questions.explanation:
The Mughal Painter- 'Bisandas' drew the
portrait of the Shah of Persia. Bisandas sent on a
diplomatic mission to Persia in 1613 where he painted
portrait of shah of Persia and other leading Persian
figures. Here he was so successful that he remained
until 1620 and on his return Jahangir gave him an
elephant.

questions.explanation:
'Mudra-rakshasam'- It is a Sanskrit play

questions.questionText:
15. Hastyayurveda which deals with the diagnosis
and treatment of the major diseases of
elephants was written by
questions.explanation:
Hastyayurveda deals with the diagonsis and
treatment of the major diseases of Elephant was written
by 'Palakapya'. The text is partly in prose and partly in
verse. It is in the form of dialogue between the Asga
king Romapada and Palakapya. This text is also Known
as 'Gajayurveda'

1712 to 1713. ]

18. Who among the following first referred to the
Chaudhuris (as Jautari) as the headman of
non-Muslim revenue payers
questions.explanation:
Ibn-Battuta- He was the first person who
referred to the Chaudhuris (as Jautari) as the headman
of non-Muslim revenue payers. Ibn battuta was traveller
from morocco (Africa). He reached India during rule of
Mohammad bin Tughlaq. In 1342, He was sent as
emmissary to china. He stayed in court of sultan of
Madurai in 1345. He published his travel account by
name 'Rihla'.

South Indian inscriptions.

E. First issue of Epigraphia indica

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below
questions.explanation:
Arrangement of the following facts in a
chronological manner are as follows:-
(A) Colin Mackenzie (or Colin Mackenzie) collects
over 8,000 inscriptions in Sanskrit and in
Dravidian language in 1810
(B) Decipherment of Ashokan Brahmi by James

Princep done in 1837.
(C) Alexander Cunningham publishes a set of

Ashokan Inscriptions in 1877.
(D) First issue of Epigraphica Carnatica, a journal of

South Indian inscriptions was published in 1886.
(E) First issue of Epigraphica Indica was published in

1888.
So, the correct answer is - A, B, C, D, E.

questions.explanation:
Nammalvar saints were the follower of the
Vaishnava tradition.
 [Nammalvar was one of the twelve (12) Alvar poet-
saints who immersed themselves in a love of Vishnu
and who had a considerable knowledge of Ancient
Tamil Literature and its variants of traditional stories
concerning Vishnu and his associates. ]

Sir Stanley Jackson, the Governor of Bengal at Calcutta
University's Convocation was belonged to "Diocesan
Women's College." Bina Das was member of Chhatri
Sangha , a semi revolutionary organisation for women

Under the leadership of Charles Aitchison,

has recommended the raising of the maximum age for

civil service examination 23 years.

Direction (91-95) : Read the passage carefully
and answer the questions that follows
The Indian monotheisits call the Vision of God,
Sachlatkar, that is, to see God with the (Ordinary) eyes
of the forehead. Know that the Vision of God, either by
the Prophets, may peace be on them, or by the perfect
divines, may their souls be sanctified, whether in this or
the next world and whether with the outer or the inner
eyes, cannot be doubed or disputed and the "men of the
Book" (ahl-i-kitab) the perfect divines and the seers of all
religions- whether they are believers in the Kuran the
Vedas, the Book of David or the Old and the New
Testaments- have a (common) faith in this respect. Now,
one who disbelieves the beholding of God is a
throughless and sightless member of his community, the
reason being. if the Holy self is Omnipotent, how can He
not have the potency to menifest Himself? This matter
has been explained very clearly by the 'Ulama of the
Sunni Sect.
But, if it is said that (even) the Pure Self (dhat-i-
baht) can be beheld. It is an impossiblity; for the Pure
Self is elegant and undetermined and as He cannot be
determined, He is mainfest in the veil of elegance only.
and as such cannot be beheld, and such beholding is an
impossibility.
And the suggestion that he can be beheld in the next
and not in this world, is groundless for if He is
Omnipotent. He is potent to manifest Himself in any
manner, anywhere, and at any time he likes. (I hold) that
one cannot behold Him here (i.e. in this world) will
hardly behold Him there (i.e. in the next world); as He
has said in the Holy verse; "And whoever is blind in this,
he shall (also) be blind in the hereafter."
The Mu'tazila and the Shia's doctors. Who are
opposed to Ruyai (Beholding), have committed a great
blunder in this matter, for had they only denied the
capability or beholding the Pure Self, there would have
been some justification, but their denial of all form of
Ruyai (i.e. Beholding) is a grat mistake.

successors of Muhammad and in the concealment and
messianic return of the last recognized Imam compare
Sunni.)

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2021/June 2022 (10.10.2022-II) Paper II

capability to
questions.explanation:

( Manifestation- A Manifestation is the public display
of emotions or feelings, or something theoretical made
real. Manifestation's origins are in religion and
spirituality because if something spiritual becomes real,
it is said to be a Manifestation.)

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
1. Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and
Jataka texts belong to which Buddhist Canon?
questions.explanation:
Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and
Jataka texts belong to Khuddaka Nikaya. Khuddaka
nikaya, the fifth division of Sutta Pitaka is a wide range
collection of fifteen Books. Five divisions of Sutta
Pitaka are Digha Nikaya, Majjhima nikaya Samyutta
Nikaya, Anguttara Nikaya and Khuddaka Nikaya.
* Pitaka are ancient Buddhist text. Pitaka are 3 in
number.
1. Sutta Pitaka largest among all Pitaka contains
Religious thought of Buddha.
2. Vinaya-Pitaka- Rules of Buddhist Sangha
3. Abhidhamma Pitaka- Philosophy of Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
2.
Which of the following texts is related to Jain
Tradition?
questions.explanation:
Paumachariyam is related to Jainism.
Paumachariyam is the earliest Jain work dealing with
the story of Rama. written by Acharya Vimalsuri in
Prakrit. Dasarath Jataka is a Jataka tale found in
Buddhist
literature
about
the
previous
life
of
Shakyamuni (Gautam Buddha). The Thai national epic
is based on Dasarath Jataka.
Iramavataram is Tamil version of Ramayana composed
by Kamban.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
3.
What was the family emblem of the Gupta
monarchs?
questions.explanation:
The family emblem of the Gupta monarchs
was Garuda. Garuda was Found on many seals of
Gupta rulers. Gupta dynasty was founded by Shri
gupta. Silver coins were issued first time during rule of
Chandragupta I.
 Largest number of coins issued by king Kumara
Gupta.
 Vincent Smith said king Samudragupta Napolean of
India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
4.
Who is the author of Prabodha-Candrodaya?
questions.explanation:
Prabodha chandrodaya is a Sanskrit play of
11th century composed by Krishna Mishra. Krishna
Mishra
was
contemporary
to
Chandela
king
Kirtivarman. This play was played in Khajuraho
complex. It contain 6 Acts. It was written to teach
Advaita doctrine to those who were interested in Kavya
not in philosophy.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
5.
The
Aitareya
and
Satpatha
Brahmanas
mention the name of which monarch, who
performed the 'Asvamedha' sacrifice along
with the 'Aindra Mahabhisek'
questions.explanation:
The Aitareya and Satapath Brahman mention
the king Para who performed the 'Asvamedha sacrifice
along with' 'Aindra Mahabhishek'. King Para was
associated with Kosala Kingdom.
* Aitareya Brahmana is Brahman text of Rigveda.
* Satpath Brahmana is Brahman text of Yajurveda.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
6.
Rajpura and Dvaraka were important town of
which region?
questions.explanation:
Rajpura and Dvaraka were important town of
Kamboja region. Kamboja was situated in the extreme
north west of India. It's capital was Dvaraka.
Mahabharata mentions the name of Rajpura.
* Avanti- Madhya pradesh
* Kuru- near delhi
* Gandhar- Afghanistan.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
7.
Ottakkuttan did not write about which of the
following king?
questions.explanation:
Ottakkuttan did not write about king Rajaraja
I. Ottakkuttion was tamil court poet of later Chola kings
Vikrama Chola, Kulotunga II and Rajaraja II. He has
written 'ula' poems for these 3 kings. ula poems were
written in honour of Kings. Rajaraja I was great king of
chola dynasty. He adopted Title of "Arimolivarman".
[Exam Date: 28.02.2023] Shift-I

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
8.
Name the inscription which refers to the
construction of a puja-sila-prakara
questions.explanation:
Ghosundi refers to the construction of puja-
sila-prakara. It is written in Brahmi script. Ghosundi
inscription is situated in Rajasthan. It confirms the
ancient reverence of Hindu deities samkarshana and
vasudeva. It was first read by D.R. Bhandarkar.
 Nanaghat inscription was inscribed by Satavahana
queen Naganika. It gives vivid picture of satavahana
dynasty
 Hathigumpha inscription of Kharvela provides info. of
events during rule of Kharvela.
 The Halmidi Inscription (Karnataka) dates back 450
A.D. and it is oldest known inscription with Kannada
character. The 16 line inscription is on rectangular
sandstone.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
9.
The Chariya-Pitaka is a collection of :
questions.explanation:
The Chariya-pitaka is a collection of 35
Jatakas in verse. Chariya Pitaka is Khuddaka Nikay'as
15th lesson. Chariya Pitaka was originally written in Pali
languge. Chariya Pitaka was composed by Bhikshu
Dharmarakshit.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 10. Lankavatara is related to
questions.explanation:
Lankavatara is related to Vaipulya sutras.
The Vaipulya sutras designate particular scripture in
Mahayana Known as dharma-s. The nine Dharma-s are
a series of books composed at different periods and
belong to different Persuassions.
nine works are 1. Astasahsrika prajnaparamita 2.
Saddharmapundarika 3. Lalita vistara 4. Lankavatara 5.
Suvarnaprabhasa 6. Gandavyuha 7. Tathagataguhyaka
8. Samadhiraja 9. Dasabhumisvara.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
11. The neolithic sites of Kiari and Giak are
located in
questions.explanation:
The Neolithic sites of Kiari and Giak are
located in Ladakh union territory. Kiari and Giak were
famous for hand made red pottery. Burjahom, chirand
etc. are other Neolithic sites in J&K.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
12. The Ghaggar-Hakra system of river is studied
by
questions.explanation:
The Ghaggar Hakra system of river is studied
by C.E. Oldham. many scholars identified Ghaggar
hakra river with the vaidic saraswati river. Ghaggar
Hakra river was intermittent between India and
Pakistan.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
13. According to A.K. Ghosh which of the
following is not a chrono-cultural element of
the palaeolithic culture complex in India?
questions.explanation:
According to A.K Ghosh Borer Burin is not a
chrono cultural element of the Paleolithic culture
complex in India. Pebble, flake and Flake blades tools
was characteristic of Paleolithic culture. In 1966 A.K.
Ghosh divided Indian Palaeolithic culture mainly in 3
parts-
1. Chopper element
2. Flake elements
3. Flake blade elements

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
14. Who among the following Rajput nobles held
the mansab of 7000/7000 under Aurangzeb?
questions.explanation:
Mirza Raja jai singh was Rajput noble who
held the mansab of 7000/7000 under Aurangzeb.
Despite of victories with all his brothers Aurangzeb did
not secured footing on Mughal throne so he needed
support of leading muslim and Rajput generals. hence
he pardoned Jaswant Singh and promoted Jai Singh as
a commander of 7000 the highest possible rank for any
general.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
15. Which one of the following texts, describes two
methods of lifting water out of wells in India?
questions.explanation:
Baburnama describes two methods of lifting
water out of wells in India. Babur wrote in Baburnama
In Lahore, Dipalpur people lift water by means of
wheel. In Agra, Chandawar, Bayana people lift water
with a bucket at the well-edge they setup fork of wood-
having a roller adjusted between the forks tie a rope to
large bucket put the rope over a roller bucket and tie it's
others and to the bullock one person must drive bullock
another empty Bucket.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
16. Who observed that while Akbar was on an
expedition to Kabul to subdue the rebellion of
Mirza Hakim, he appointed his mother,
Hamida Banu Begam, in charge of the suba of
Delhi.
questions.explanation:
Father Anthony Monserrate observed that
while Akbar was on an expedition to Kabul to subdue
the rebellion of Mirza Hakim he appointed his mother
Hamida Bano Begam in charge of the suba of Delhi.
Father Monserrate reached in Akbar's court with father
Aquaviva
of
Portugal.
Akbar
appointed
father
Monserrate as teacher of prince Murad.
Father Monserrate accompanied Akbar on his military
expedition to Kabul in 1581. Father Monserrate
remained at Akbar's court untill April 1582.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
17. In
January
171,
Muzaffar
Jang
was
accompanied by a French force under the
leadership of which one of the following
commanders.
questions.explanation:
In January 1751- Muzaffar Jang was
accompanied by a French force under the leadership of
captain Bussy. In second carnatic war French East India
company supported Muzaffar Jung's claim on throne in
Hyderabad and chanda sahib's claim on carnatic throne.
French sent force in commandership of Bussy. IInd
Carnatic war extended from 1749-54 A.D.
This war ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
18. In early modern period, who was known as
"Ummal'?
questions.explanation:
In early modern period 'Ummal' was Tax
collector.
Some, other important terms
Muqaddam – village headman Abwab – cess
Diwan-i-wizarat – Finance department
Ghari – House tax
Fawazil – Surplus amount
Muqti – Iqta holder.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
19. Saranjam, assignment of revenue from villages
to support military service, was a popular
practice under which Empire?
questions.explanation:
Saranjam assignment of revenue from
villages to support military service was popular practice
under Maratha empire.
Saranjam system was like Jagir system the land was
mostly in the form of rural watan. its owner being
entitled to extract revenue from the villages included in
territory. Saranjam usually given that person for heroic
deeds in military field.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
20. Who
wrote
'Time
is
precious
and
is
irreplaceable"?
questions.explanation:
"Time is precious and is irreplaceable"
written by Abul Fazal.
Abul fazal was among nine lewels of Akbar. Abul Fazal
composed Akbarnama in 3 volumes. Third volume Ain-
i-Akbari is his most famous book. It contained detailed
report of Akbar's government and administration.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
21. Who stated that the days of Nur Jahan were
revived for her (Lal Kunwar) and coins were
issued in her name?
questions.explanation:
Hadi kamwar khan stated that the Days of
Nur Jahan were revived for her (Cal kunwar) and coins
were issued in her name. Hadi kamwar khan added a
continuation to Jahangir's memoir from 1624 (where
motmid khan stopped) and death in 1627. He was
contemporary of Aurangzeb.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
22. Which one of the following sites in Rajasthan
provides evidence of the onset of aridity around
2000 B.C.
questions.explanation:
Lunkaransar site in Rajasthan provides
evidence of the onset of aridity around 2000 B.C.
Lunkaransar is located in Bikaner District.
Lunkaransar is a Playa lake. Migratory birds came here
in winter season.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
23. The Court of Directors withheld their sanction
to the annexation of which princely state on the
basis of 'Doctrine of Lapse'.
questions.explanation:
The court of Directors withheld their sanction
to the annexation of Karauli princely state on the basis
of doctrine of Lapse. Karauli princely state was in
Rajasthan. Princely state of Karauli was established by
Raja Bijai pal, a yaduvanshi Rajput around 995 A.D
Last ruler of Karauli was Maharaja Ganesh pal deo.
* Satara was first princely state annexed by Doctrine of
Lapse in 1848.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
24. Which Indian Factories Act provided for a
weekly holiday for all workers?
questions.explanation:
The second Indian factory act 1891 provided
for a weekly holidays for all workers. Other provisions
of second factory act
* Minimum age for the employment of children raised
from seven to nine years
* To secure to woman and children proper intervals for
food and rest during day
* To limit the employment of women to eleven hours a
day.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
25. What was the immediate cause for the first
burmese war (1824-6)?
questions.optionA:
The declaration of cachar as a British
protectorate
questions.optionB:
The establishment of political authority by
Burma in Manipur
questions.optionC: The British naval mission in Rangoon
questions.optionD: The British expedition in Misami hills
questions.explanation:
The Immediate cause of EirstAnglo Burmese
war (1824-26) was the declaration of Cachar as a
British Protectorate. The war ended with Treaty of
Yandabo (1820).
Important conditions of treaty
* Pay rupee one crore as war compensation.
* Abandon claims on Assam, Cachar and Jaintia
* Recognise Manipur as an Independent state.
* Accept a British resident at Ava while posting a
Burmese envoy at Calcutta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
26. Who wrote the essay 'Gandhiji's Leadership and
the Congress Socialist Party'?
questions.explanation:
"Gandhi ji's Leadership and the congress
socialist party" essay was written by Jaiprakash
Narayan. Congress socialist party was founded in 1934
by Jaiprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia and
Acharya Narendra Dev. It declared it would act under
the aegis of INC. It's primary objective was to Outroot
British imperialism and empowerment of labourers,
farmers and other Vulnerable class of the society.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
27. The celebrated diamond, the Koh-i-Noor, was
surendered to the British crown after which
war?
questions.explanation:
The celebrated diamond Koh-i-Noor was
surrendered to the British crown after Second Anglo-
Sikh war. Second Anglo Sikh war was fought between
Sikhs & British army in 1848-1849. At that time
governor general was Lord Dalhousie. Charles Napier
commander of British army defeated Sikhs in "battle of
Gujarat." Punjab was annexed in British territory
maharaja Daleep Singh sent to London with anuual
pension of 50000 pound.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
28. As a prominent leader of the 1928 scavengers'
strike who was given the epithet 'Dhangarma'
(Mother of Scavengers)
questions.explanation:
As a prominent leader of the 1928 scavengers
strike Prabhabati Das Gupta was given the epithet
"Dhangarma". on 5 March 1928 8000 scavengers went
on strike in Calcutta. Their demands were wage
increase, suitable housing and accommodation 15 days
leave per year. medical benefits and free primary
education for their children. Strike was settled by J.M.
Sengupta Mayor of Culcutta.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 29. 'Estado Da India's is popularly known as :
questions.explanation:
Estado Da India' is popularly known as
Portuguese east India company. Estado Da India was
the mane the Portuguese to that part of their empire
which stretched from India to east Asia. Estado Da
India formed in 1505 A.D. Francisco De Almeida
appointed as first viceroy of Portuguese company.
Almeida's vision was to make the Portuguese the master
of Indian Ocean. His policy was known as "Blue water
policy".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
30. In late 1770s and 1780s Khatbandi regulations
were related to :
questions.optionA:
Indian peasants to buy their agricultural tools
from the British East India Company
questions.optionB:
Bind Indian artisans to sell their products
exclusively to the British East India company
questions.optionC:
Bind Indian peasants to pay their land
revenue in each to the British East India
Company
questions.optionD:
Indian artisans to buy their raw material like
cotton exclusively from the British East India
Company
questions.explanation:
In late 1770s and 1780s khatbandi regulations
were related to Bind Indian Artisans to sell their
products exclusively to the British East India company.
Thus the Artisans were reduced step by step to the
position of Bonded laborers by the denial of free Access
to market by the use of coercion and by laws and
regulations made by company's government. Khatbandi
regulations were passed by Bengal Govt.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
31. Dada Bhai Naoroji presented the case of 'drain
of wealth' from India before which Commission
in 1895.
questions.explanation:
Dada bhai Naoroji presented the case of drain
of wealth from India before welby commission. welby
commission was established by British government In
year 1895 under official name 'Royal commission on
expenditure Administration of India' Main objective of
commission was to find out the income and expenditure
of the nation. Dadabhai Naoroji was the commissions
first Indian member.
 Macdonald Commission – 1900 by curzon to enquire
into the Famine of 1873-74 in Bengal & Bihar.
 Strachey Commission– 1880 first famine commission.
It was established to develop general strategy to tackle
famines.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
32. The Fergusson college was developed from
which institution of 1880s
questions.explanation:
The Fergusson college was developed from
New English school of 1880s. In 1880 V.K. Chiplunkar,
Balgangadhar Tilak and M.B. Namjoshi started new
English school in Pune with the objective of cheapening
and facilitating education. The founders of the
Fergusson college had first started the new English
school, Pune in 1880 and Later established the 'Deccan
Education society in 1884. Fergusson College was
started in 1885.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
33. Who was the President of the 1929 Congress
sub-committee on untouchability?
questions.explanation:
Pandit madan mohan Malaviya was the
president of the 1929 congress sub committee on
untouchability.
Madan Mohan Malviya was educationist social
reformer and freedom fighter. He was elected as the
president of the congress committee (Four times) in
1909, 1918, 1932 and 1933. Mahatma Gandhi gave him
title of 'Mahamana'. Dr. S. Radha Krishnan gave him
status of Karmayogi. He founded Hindu Mahasabha in
1905. He founded Banaras Hindu university in 1916.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
34.
Who was the Propounder of the theory of
'Utilitarianism'?
questions.explanation:
J.S. Mill was Propounder of the theory of
'utilitarianism'. Utilitarianism was a developed in
Britain. Main objective of utilitarianism is "maximum
satisfaction for maximum number of people."

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 35. Where was Herodotus born?
questions.explanation:
Herodotus was born in Halicarnassus. now in
Turkey. Herodotus is known as "Father of history".
Herodotus earned this title from Roman statesman.
Cicro because he authored the first authoritative
historical text that systematically recorded historical
events. Herodotus wrote books the Histories and The
tale of the great Persian war.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
36. Leni Riefenstahl's film Triumph of the will
deals with ___________.
questions.explanation:
Triumph of the will is a 1935 German Nazi
propaganda film directed and produced by Leni
Riefenstahl's. It chronicles the 1934 Nazi party congress
in Nuremberg. Which was attended by more than
700000 Nazi Supporters. The film contains excerpts
speeches given by Nazi leaders at the congress
including Hitler.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
37. Who said, "As works of the imagination, the
historian's work and the novelist's do not
differ. Where they do differ is that the
historian's picture is meant to be true".
questions.explanation:
R.G. Collingwood said "As works of the
Imagination. the historian's work and the novelist's do
not differ. where they do differ is that the historian's
picture is meant to be true."
R.G. Collingwood was great historian from England. He
is best known for his works "The principles of Art
(1938) and the posthumously Published" "The Idea of
History".

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
38. Who said "History has to be rewritten because
history is the selection of those threads of causes
or antecedents that we are interested in".
questions.explanation:
Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. said "History has
to be rewritten because history is the selection of those
threads of causes or antecedents that we are interested
in". Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. was an American Jurist
who served as an associate justice of the supreme court
of the united states from 1902-1932.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText: 39. Ramoshi Rebellion of 1831 was led by whom?
questions.explanation:
Ramoshi Rebellion of 1831 was led by Umaji
Raje. Ramosis, the hill tribe of western ghat resented
the policy of Annexation after the Annexation of
Maratha territories by British. The Ramosis who had
been employed by Maratha administration, lost their
means of livelihood they rose under chittur Singh in
1822. from 1825-26 to 1831 Ramosi rebellion was led
by Umaji Raje

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
40. Raja Rammohan Roy's Brahmo Samaj was a
successor to :
questions.explanation:
Raja Rammohan Roy's Brahmo samaj was a
successor to Atmiya Sabha. In 1814 Raja Rammohan
Roy set up Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta to propagate the
monotheistic ideals of the Vedanta and to campaign
against Idolatary. Caste rigidities, meaningless rituals
and other social ills. In 1828 he founded Brahmo samaj.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:

about Tarikh/Tawarikh during the Medieval
period?

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
42. Regarding to the role of European Trading
Companies which of the following statements
are correct?

A. In 1605, the Dutch captured the Portuguese
fort of Ambonia

B. In 1606, Dutch obtained a farman from the
ruler of Golconda to setup a factory at
Masulipatam.

C. The Dutch opened their factory at Surat in
1617.

D. English had already opened a factory at
Surat in 1625

E. The Dutch captured Malacca in 1639.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :

Statement (A) (B) and (C) are correct

Statement (D) is incorrect because English opened a
factory at Surat in1613 not in 1625.
statement (E) is incorrect because Dutch captured
Malacca in 1641 not in 1639

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
43. Which of the following are correct?

A. The Vayu Purana refers to Vindhyasakti,
founder of Vakataka dynasty and his son
Pravira.

B. In early epigraphic records the Abhiras
figure
as
General
of
the
Saka
Mahakshatrapas of Western india.

C. The Ikshvakus mentioned in the Kautilya
Arthashastra, ruled from the city of
Madurai.

D. The Bodhi dynasty flourished in territory
that was once within the sphere of Chera.

E. The Mahavamsa does not mentioned Chola
king Karikala invasion of Cylone.

Choose the correct answer from the option
given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (E) are correct
statement (c) is not correct because. Ikshvakus ruled in
India's eastern krishna river valley from their capital at
Vijayapuri (modern Nagarjunankonda in Andhra
Pradesh)
Statement (D) is not correct because Bodhi Dynasty was
successor of Satavahana Dynasty not of Chera Dynasty.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
44. Which out of these are correct

A. Brihadisvara Temple in Tanjavur was
built by the Chola kings.

B. The walls of the temple have the paintings
of the Chola kings.

C. Tripurantaka is another name of Siva

D. Rajarajeshwar Temple symbolises a great
phase of art of Chola dynasty.

E. Rajaraja was a devotee of goddess Durga.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Brihadishvara temple in Tanjavur was built
by chola king Rajaraja. The wall of temple depicts
portrait of Rajaraja worshiping god Shiva. Tripurantaka
is another name of shiva. Rajarajeshwar temple
symbolizes great phase of art of chola dynasty. Rajaraja
was devotee of shiva but a painting of Goddess Durga
found from Brihadisvara temple. Hence all statement
are correct, N.T.A Dropped this question.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
45. Which of the following are correct?

A. Nagarjunkonda inscription dates to year
278 C.E.

B. Nagarjunkonda
inscription
records
dedication
to
the
image
of
Devaparamadeva.

C. Abhir King Vaisisthiputra Vasushena was
a devotee of goddess Durga.

D. The Nagarjunakonda inscription records
the supreme god as the primordial male

E. Nagarjunkonda inscription also described
the god as Rumbara-bhava

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B), (D) and (E) are correct.
Nagarjunakonda inscription dates to year 278 CE. It is
related to Ikshvakus. It records dedication of the image
of Deva Paramadeva. This inscription records the
supreme god as primordial male. This inscription also
describes the god as Rumbara bhava.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
46. Regarding the condition of servants and slaves,
which of the following statements are correct?

A. Moreland dwells upon slavery in his 'India
at the Death of Akbar'

B. Firuz Tughlaq was the only one who used
slaves for manufacturing purposes

C. The Portuguese employed slaves on a large
scale.

D. The pilgrim ships to Jeddah did not
indulge in slave trade.

E. Akbar allowed the practice of enslaving
prisoners of war.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (C) are correct
regarding the condition of servants and slaves.
Statement (D) is not correct because pilgrim ships to
Jeddah were indulge in slave trade
Statement (E) is not correct because Akbar stopped
enslaving prisoners of war and forcible conversion of
prisoners of wars in Islam.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
47. Which statements are correct in reference to
the Treaty of Purandar (1665)?

A. Out of 35 forts held by Shivaji, 23 forts
were to be surrendered to the Mughals.

B. The surrendered forts yielded a revenue of
four lakhs Huns every year.

C. The remaining 12 forts yielding an annual
income of two lakhs Huns were to be left to
Shivaji.

D. A territory in the Bijapuri Konkan was
granted to Shivaji.

E. Shivaji had to pay 30 lakh Huns in
installments to the Mughals.

Choose the most apprpriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B) and (D) are correct in
reference to the Treaty of Purandar (1665). Treaty of
Purandar was signed between Raja Jai singh and shivaji.
conditions of Treaty of Purandar
1. Shiva ji surrendered 23 forts to mughals
2. Surrendered forts yielded revenue of 4 Lakh Huns
every year.
3. only 12 forts remains with Shivaji
4. Mughal accepted to give Sambhaji mansab of 5000.
5. A territory in Bijapuri konkan was granted to shivaji.
6. Shivaji promised mughals to help against Bijapur.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
48. Regarding the trade in Medieval period, which
statements are correct?

A. Salt was brought to the capital from
Kanauj, Kara and Manikpur.

B. Betel-leaf was imported from North-
Eastern part.

C. Delhi obtained supplies from fairly distant
rural regions.

D. Barani elaborately mentions Alauddin
Khilji's
agrarian
and
price
control
measures.

E. Ibn Battuta tells us that grain was mainly
supplied from Amroha, situated on the
banks of Ganga.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (C), (D) and (E) are correct
regarding trade in medieval period that Delhi obtained
supplies from fairly distant rural regions. Barani
mentions Allauddin khilji's agrarian and price control
measures. Ibn battuta tells as that grain was mainly
supplied from Amroha.
* Ibn battuta also mentioned mango in his account
* Alauddin
tried
to
control
price
of
essential
commodities.
* According to Barani Alauddin set up 3 markets one
for food grain, second for cloth & expensive items,
third for horses, silver and cattle.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
49. Which of these are correct?

A. On 18 February 1946 the naval rating
started protest on H.M.I.S. Talwar.

B. The main reason for naval mutiny in
Bombay
was
bad
food
and
racial
discrimination.

C. Bombay city was silent during the Naval
mutiny and people's participation in strike
was not there.

D. A Maratha battalion was called in to bring
peace to Bombay.

E. Hartal also happened in Karachi in
February 1946.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.optionD: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (B), (D) and E are correct
regarding Naval mutiny 1946.
on 18 February 1946 the ratings of HMIS Talwar in
Bombay harbour went into hunger Strike to protest
against bad food and worst racial arrogance. on 22 Feb
revolt had spread to all the naval bases in the country. In
Karachi the Hindes and muslim students and workers
demonstrated in support of ratings. Bombay witnessed
emotional expression of public sympathy people hailing
the ratings, rushing in food for them and shopkeepers
insisting on their taking whatever articles they liked.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
50. Which of these are correct?

A. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar joined as a Professor
at Sydenham College

B. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded Independent
Labour Party.

C. Independent Labour Party had a red flag.

D. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar himself did not
support a non-Aryan theory of dalit-
shudra identity

E. In 1936, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar published the
book 'The Annihilation of Caste'.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.optionD: A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation:
B.R. Ambedkar was born on April 14, 1891
Ambedkar got school education from satara He
completed his graduation from Elphinstone college
Bombay. He got his M.A. and Ph.D. from Columbia
university. Ambedkar joined Sydenham college as a
professor of political economy. He published Bahiskrit
Bharat newspaper, Ambedkar founded Independent
Labour party in 1936. Its flag have red colour.
Ambedkar did not supported a non-Aryan theory of
dalit-shudra identity. In 1936 they published book "The
Annihilation of caste". In 1956 Ambedkar embraced
Buddhism.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
51. Which of the following are correct?

A. The adoption of resolution of Boycott and
Swadeshi took place at a meeting in Town
Hall, Calcutta.

B. Khudiram Bose was executed on 30th April,
1908.

C. The Arundel Committee submitted its
report to Lord Irwin.

D. Shyamaji Krishnavarma founded the India
Home Rule Society in London in February
1906.

E. Madan Lal Dhingra shot dead Curzon
Wyllie in London on 1st July 1909.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below.
questions.explanation:
Statement (A) and E are correct. Resolution
of Boycott and Swadeshi took place in meeting in town
hall, Calcutta. madan lal Dhingra shat dead Curzon
wyllie in London on Ist July 1909, statement (B) is not
correct because Khudiram Bose was executed on 11
August 1908.
Statement (C) is not correct because Arundel committee
on political reform submitted it's report to Lord Minto
not to Lord Irwin.
Statement (D) is not correct because shyamaji Krishna
verma founded the India Home Rule society in London
in 1905 not in 1906.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:

A. Since 1770, even before Cornwallis arrived,
company officials, like Alexander Dow,
Henry Patullo and Philip Francis were
advocating for land tax being permanently
fixed.

B. Physiocratic school assigned primacy to
agriculture in country's economy.

C. Introduction of Permanent settlement led
assessment forever.

D. The assessment under the permanent
settlement would reduce the scope of
corruption.

E. It was hoped that under the Permanent
settlement the landlord will not invest in
improving the land.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, B, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Since 1770 even before Cornwallis arrived
company officials like Alexander dow. Henry Patullo
and Philip Francis were advocating for land tax being
permanently
fixed.
physiocratic
school
assigned
primacy to agriculture in country's economy. permanent
settlement. introduced by Cornwallis in 1793 in Bengal,
Bihar, odisa and Benaras region of u.p. Introduction of
permanent settlement led to assessment forever. The
assessment under permanent settlement would reduce
scope of corruption It was hoped that in permanent
settlement the landlord will invest in improving land.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
53. Which of these are correct

A. The Hindi-Urdu controversy began in the
North-Western
provinces
and
Awadh
sometime in the 1860s.

B. The movement acquired greater intensity
in 1890s with the foundation of the 'Nagri
Pracharani Sabha' in 1893.

C. Hindi was written in Devnagari script so it
has greater sprinkling of Sanskrit words.

D. Urdu was written in Persian script thus
had more Persian and Arabic words.

E. In April 1900 a Resolution of the
Government of North Western province
and Awadh gave Nagari an equal official
status with Sanskrit.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the
options given below :
questions.optionC: A, B, C and D only
questions.optionD: A, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
In 1867 Hindus in united provinces of Agra
and Oudh began to demand that Hindi be made an
official language in place of Urdu, Babu Shiva Prasad
was one of early proponents of Nagari script, movement
intensified after establishment of Nagari Pracharini
Sabha in Benaras in 1893. Hindi was written in
Devnagari script so it has greater sprinkling of Sanskrit
words. Urdu was written in Persia script thus had more
Persian and Arabic words.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
54. Which of the following statement are NOT
correct.

A. Dara Shikoh translated the Upanishads
into Persian language.

B. This project was completed in the year
1657 CE.

C. Dara Shikoh oversees the translation of
Yoga Vashisht in 1860.

D. Dara-Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar is a Persian
introduction to Bhagvad Gita.

E. Majma al-Bahrain was not written by
Dara Shikoh.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below.
questions.optionA: A, B, D and E only
questions.optionB: B, C, D and E only
questions.explanation:
Dara shikoh was son of Shahjahan he
translated fifty Upanishads into Persian language
translation of Upanishad was known as 'sirr-i-Akbar'
(The greatest mystery). This project was completed in
the year 1657 CE. His book Majma-ul-Bahrain was
devoted to a revelation of the mystical and pluralistic
affinities between Sufic & Vedantic. He commissioned
translation of Yoga Vasistha in 1006 A.H.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
55. Which of the following is correct?

A. Samkaracharya's Prasthanatrayi includes
Upanishads,
Brahmasutra
and
the
Bhagavad Gita.

B. Samkaracharya was a disciple of Mandana
Mishra.

C. Jyeshteshwar
temple
is
situated
in
Srinagar.

D. Samkaracharya was called a crypto-
Buddhist (Pracchanna Baudha) by his
intellectual opponents.

E. Samkaracharya went to Mandana Mishra
for a philosophical debate.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below.
questions.explanation:
Samkaracharya was born in Kerala. He was
disciple of Govindacharya. He Propounded theory of
Advaita
Vedanta.
Samkaracharya's
Prasthanatrayi
includes Upanishads, Brahmasutra and Bhagvad Gita.
Samkaracharya
went
to
Mandana
Mishra
for
philosophical debate. Samkaracharya was called a
crypto
Buddhist
(Pracchanna
Bauddha)
by
his
intellectual opponents. Jyeshteshwar temple is situated
in Srinagar It is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
56. Which statement from below are correct?

A. A Buddhist believes in the three Buddha,
Dhamma and Samgha to seek nirvana.

B. Sariputra and Tathagata are two different
people.

C. Both the Theravadins and Mahayanist
believe in the teachings of the Buddha.

D. The Buddha delivered his first sermon in
Bodhagaya.

E. Ashoka's Lion capital was first installed in
Sarnath, near Varanasi.

Choose the correct answer from the options
given below :
questions.explanation:
Statement (A), (C) and E are correct.
Buddhism was founded by Siddharth (Gautam Buddha).
Buddhism believes in three jewels Buddha, Dhamma
and Sangha to seek nirvana. Buddha delivered his first
sermon in Sarnath. Sariputra was chief disciple of
Buddha, Ashoka's Lion capital was first installed in
Sarnath near Varanasi Lion capital of Ashoka is
national Amblem of India.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:

treaty concluded between Maharaja Jai Singh
and Prince Muhammad Azam?

Mandal, Pur and Badnor to the Mughals.

B. In lieu of the above, Jiziya was imposed in

Choose the correct answer from the options

Staement (B), (D) and (E) are incorrect about
treaty between Jaisingh and Mohammad Azam.
Mohammad Azam and Jaisingh signed a Treaty on 24
June 1651.
Conditions of treaty
1. Jaisingh surrendered Pur, mandal and Badnor
Pargana to Mughal king for avoiding zijya tax.
2. Mughal king will not interrupt Mewar.
3. Jaisigh will not support Rathors
4. Jaisingh got Mansab of 5000.

questions.testName: UGC NTA NET/JRF History Dec 2022 (28.02.2023, Shift-I) Paper II
questions.questionText:
58. Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The Chandela ruler, Yasovarman
constructed
the
Lakshmana
(Vaikuntha)
temple at Khajuraho for Vaikuntha Vishnu,
which he obtained from the Pratihara ruler,
Devapala.

Statement
II
:
The
Kalachuri
King,
Lakshmanaraja I obtained from the king of
Vigraha dynasty an image of krishna.

In the light of the above statements, choose the
correct answer from the options given below :
questions.optionA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.optionB: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
questions.optionC:
Statement I is the true but Statement II is
false.
questions.optionD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

statement (II) is incorrect that the kalchuri king
